item.title: Cationic Phenylpyridine Labeling for Improved Oligosaccharide and Glycan Analysis by Capillary Electrophoresis with LED-Induced Fluorescence Detection
item.description:
Abstract
Capillary electrophoresis with laser-induced fluorescence detection (CE/LIF) is a powerful technique for analyzing glycans. However, it requires derivatization with a fluorescent compound to enhance both electrophoretic mobility and detection sensitivity simultaneously. The widely used labeling reagent 8-aminopyrene-1,3,6-trisulfonic acid (APTS) suffers from several limitations, including relatively low labeling efficiency and poor compatibility with mass spectrometry (MS), highlighting the need for improved alternatives. In this work, we designed and synthesized a novel cationic fluorescent label based on a phenylpyridine scaffold incorporating hydrazide functionality for efficient oligosaccharide and glycan derivatization via hydrazone formation. To fully exploit its fluorescence characteristics, we also optimized the capillary electrophoresis system by modifying the LED-induced fluorescence (LED-IF) detector through systematic evaluation of excitation LEDs and emission filters, resulting in substantially improved detection sensitivity. The optimized labeling, separation, and detection conditions enabled sensitive analysis of released glycans from various glycoproteins with detection limits in the nanomolar concentration range. The combination of this new phenylpyridine-based fluorescent label with the enhanced CE/LED-IF detection platform significantly improves the analytical performance of CE for glycan analysis and provides a more sensitive, robust, and versatile approach for comprehensive oligosaccharide and glycan characterization.

item.title: Ultrasound-Assisted Extraction of Bioactive Compounds from Acmella oleracea L. Leaves: Optimization by Response Surface Methodology and Comparison with Percolation
item.description:
Abstract
The extract of Acmella oleracea L. (jambu) contains significant amounts of spilanthol and phenolic compounds, which have wide-ranging applications in the cosmetic and pharmaceutical industries. The objective of this study was to optimize ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE) of hydroethanolic extracts from A. oleracea L. using a Box–Behnken factorial design combined with response surface methodology and to directly compare the results with those of the conventional percolation method. The effects of the ethanol-to-water ratio, extraction time, and solid-to-solvent ratio were evaluated on yield, total phenolic content, total flavonoid content, and antioxidant activity. In addition, Fourier-transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy was used for chemical characterization and extraction monitoring. For UAE, the optimal conditions established were an ethanol/water ratio of 47:53 (v/v), an extraction time of 13.2 min, and a solid-to-solvent ratio of 1:10 (m/v). In contrast, optimal percolation yielded an 11.03% recovery using a 70:30 (v/v) ethanol/water ratio. UAE provided a significantly higher yield (17.61%) and better recovery of bioactive compounds, as well as superior antioxidant activity in all assays. FT-IR analysis confirmed the preservation of functional groups, demonstrating that UAE optimizes the recovery of oxygen-containing compounds. It is concluded that UAE is a green, rapid, and sustainable alternative that maximizes the potential of A. oleracea L. for future cosmetic and nutritional formulations.

item.title: Development and In Vitro Evaluation of Kaempferol-Loaded Liposomes in LN-229 Glioblastoma Cells: Potency, Selectivity, and Modulation of ROS-Dependent Cytotoxicity
item.description:
Abstract
Glioblastoma multiforme has a median survival of 12–15 months despite multimodal treatment, due to blood-brain barrier impermeability limiting CNS drug bioavailability. Liposomal nanoformulations circumvent this barrier while offering tunable surface chemistry and amphiphilic drug-loading capacity. Here, we report encapsulation of kaempferol, a dietary flavonoid, within phosphatidylcholine-cholesterol liposomes (Lip-KPF) and evaluate cytotoxic activity against LN-229 glioblastoma cells relative to free kaempferol (KPF) and puromycin aminonucleoside (Puro-A). LCMS confirmed 56% encapsulation efficiency; dynamic light scattering yielded a zeta potential of −15.32 ± 0.83 mV, mean particle size of 200.44 ± 12.22 nm, and PDI of 0.29 ± 0.06, with 31P NMR confirming a multilamellar structure. Lip-KPF potency against LN-229 cells increased progressively across 24–72 h, peaking at 72 h (19.880 μM) with significantly lower IC50 values than free KPF (p < 0.001), while maintaining lower astrocyte toxicity. Selectivity indices for Lip-KPF exceeded 1 at every time point, widening over time. Cell death was confirmed by TUNEL assay and phase-contrast microscopy. RT-qPCR revealed concurrent BAX and TP53 upregulation alongside CASP3/CASP7 suppression in both groups, with no significant difference between KPF and Lip-KPF; ELISA corroborated CASP3 suppression, consistent with a possible caspase-independent death mechanism. In a preliminary antioxidant rescue assay, pretreatment did not significantly alter KPF-induced cytotoxicity but significantly increased it in Lip-KPF-treated cells, indicating a cytotoxic mechanism independent of the ROS pathway contributing to free KPF’s activity. These findings support Lip-KPF as a candidate for continued preclinical investigation in LN-229 glioblastoma cells.

item.title: Enhanced Shale-Swelling Inhibition and Plugging Efficiency in Water-Based Drilling Muds by Graphene Oxide Nanocomposites
item.description:
Abstract
Shale formations pose significant challenges to conventional water-based muds (WBMs) due to fluid invasion, cuttings dispersion, shale hydration and swelling, leading to wellbore instability. To address these challenges, a novel dodecylamine graphene oxide nanocomposite (DAGONC) was synthesized as a shale inhibitor. Its performance in mitigating shale hydration and enhancing the plugging efficiency of WBMs was systematically evaluated through linear swelling, API filtration, uniaxial compressive strength, contact angle, atomic force microscopy (AFM), and BET analyses. The performance of DAGONC was compared with KCl and partially hydrolyzed polyacrylamide (PHPA) inhibitors. FTIR, XRD, and FESEM confirmed successful synthesis and characterization of DAGONC. The linear swelling test showed that 0.5 wt % DAGONC reduced shale swelling to 3.6%, compared to 9.8% and 6.0% for 5 wt % KCl and 5 wt % PHPA, respectively. In addition, shale cuttings recovery at 250 °F reached to 96% with DAGONC, outperforming KCl (84%) and PHPA (90.7%). The findings showed that incorporating DAGONC into WBMs reduced fluid loss by 55% under LPLT conditions and by 38% at HPHT conditions, showing a significant enhancement in filtration control. DAGONCS increased shale surface hydrophobicity, with a contact angle of 85.6°, versus 54.6° and 63.1° for KCl and PHPA, respectively. AFM revealed a thin and homogeneous DAGONC layer bridging pores and cracks, while BET analysis indicated a reduced surface area to 6.63 m2, confirming strong interaction between DAGONC and the shale matrix. The flexible sheet-like structure forms a continuous protective film, effectively sealing pores, inhibiting water invasion, and maintaining shale integrity. These findings suggest that DAGONC can improve WBM performance and contribute to enhanced wellbore stability in shale formations.

item.title: UV-Electrochemical Catalytic Oxidation of Quinoline-Containing Wastewater Using an IrO 2 -Based Anode: COD Reduction, Degradation Kinetics, and Transformation Pathway
item.description:
Abstract
Quinoline is a refractory nitrogen-containing pollutant commonly found in coal chemical, coking, pharmaceutical, and dye wastewater. Although advanced oxidation processes have shown potential for quinoline removal, an integrated understanding of pollutant removal, COD reduction, degradation kinetics, and intermediate transformation in UV-electrochemical systems remains limited. In this study, simulated quinoline-containing wastewater was treated using a dual-wavelength UV-electrochemical catalytic oxidation system equipped with a commercial Ti/IrO2 anode and a stainless-steel cathode. The effects of current density, electrolysis time, NaCl concentration, and initial pH on quinoline degradation were systematically investigated, while COD reduction, degradation kinetics, and intermediate transformation were further evaluated by HPLC and GC-MS. Under a current density of 30 mA/cm2, NaCl concentration of 0.5 mol/L, near-neutral initial pH, and reaction time of 90 min, quinoline and COD removal efficiencies reached 87.2% and 84.7%, respectively. Further increases in current density or reaction time produced only limited additional improvement under the investigated conditions. Control experiments showed higher quinoline removal in the combined process than in either individual process. Kinetic analysis showed that quinoline degradation could be adequately described by an apparent pseudo-first-order model. HPLC and GC-MS analyses indicated a proposed transformation pathway involving hydroxylation and quinolinone formation, followed by cleavage of the aromatic and heterocyclic structures and subsequent oxidation to small-molecule organic acids. These results provide an integrated evaluation of quinoline removal, COD reduction, kinetic behavior, and intermediate transformation, thereby providing a basis for further optimization of UV-electrochemical treatment of quinoline-containing wastewater.

item.title: Docking Simulation and Artificial-Intelligence-Assisted Molecularly Imprinted Polymer Electrochemical Sensor for the Detection of Cancer Biomarkers
item.description:
Abstract
Cancer remains one of the leading life-threatening diseases worldwide, and therefore, early stage detection of cancer biomarkers is vital for effective diagnosis and treatment planning. Conventional detection techniques primarily rely on biological recognition elements, including enzymes, antibodies, aptamers, DNA, RNA; however, these elements are often prone to denaturation and have limited stability under extreme environmental conditions and long-term storage. To overcome these obstacles, molecularly imprinted polymers have emerged as a promising alternative to traditional biorecognition elements because of the ease of synthesis, low expenditure, and relative stability. In addition, MIP-based electrochemical sensors prove their applicability in detecting various disease biomarkers in general and cancer biomarkers in particular. This study presents an overview of MIPs and MIP-based electrochemical sensors, with a particular focus on their application in cancer biomarkers detection. Representative studies are discussed in detail to illustrate the structure and efficacy of these systems. In particular, strategies for improving imprinting factors of the molecular docking and artificial-intelligence-assisted MIP-electrochemical sensors up to 6.45- or 3-fold higher compared to the conventional approaches are considered in detail. Finally, current limitations and challenges, as well as future perspectives and potential solutions, are critically discussed and proposed.

item.title: Palladium(II)-Diphosphine/Lapachol complexes: Structural Insights and Selective Activity against Cisplatin-Resistant Ovarian Cancer
item.description:
Abstract
Here, we have developed and structurally characterized a series of palladium(II) complexes combining diphosphine ligands and the natural product lapachol (lap), namely [Pd(dppp)(lap)]PF6 (1), [Pd(dppb)(lap)]PF6 (2), and [Pd(dppf)(lap)]PF6 (3), where dppp = 1,3-bis(diphenylphosphino)propane, dppb = 1,4-bis(diphenylphosphino)butane, and dppf = 1,1′-bis(diphenylphosphino)ferrocene, to explore structure–activity relationships in anticancer systems. The complexes [Pd(dppp)(lap)]PF6 (1), [Pd(dppb)(lap)]PF6 (2), and [Pd(dppf)(lap)]PF6 (3) were synthesized and structurally characterized. X-ray diffraction confirmed O,O-chelation of lap and square-planar geometry around the Pd(II) center. Biological evaluation revealed that the activity of the complexes strongly depended on the diphosphine ligand. The ferrocenyl-containing complex 3 displayed remarkable cytotoxicity and selectivity toward ovarian cancer cells, particularly toward the cisplatin-resistant A2780cis line, outperforming cisplatin. Mechanistic studies demonstrated that complex 3 induced apoptosis in a concentration-dependent manner, as evidenced by morphological changes, inhibited colony formation, and cell cycle arrest in the sub-G1 phase, while activity in 3D tumor spheroid models was retained. On the basis of these results, complex 3 was effective under physiologically relevant conditions. DNA-binding experiments suggested that complexes 1–3 interacted with DNA weakly via groove binding rather than classical covalent mechanisms. Moderate to strong binding of the complexes to human serum albumin supported that they can potentially be transported in biological media. Overall, these findings highlight the critical role played by the diphosphine ligand in modulating the biological activity of the complexes and identify complex 3 as a promising candidate for developing new metallodrugs to target resistant tumors via mechanisms that differ from the mechanisms of platinum-based agents.

item.title: Wastewater-Based Epidemiological Determination of Substances Used during the Super Bowl and Mardi Gras in New Orleans, Louisiana
item.description:
Abstract
The unprecedented rise in drug overdose mortality over the past decade highlights the severity of ongoing public health crisis in the United States. Increasing polysubstance use involving synthetic fentanyl, psychostimulants, prescription opioids, veterinary tranquilizers, and nitazenes has further exacerbated this crisis, largely due to their unpredictable composition and pharmacological effects. Wastewater-based epidemiology was utilized to quantify 22 drug residues and metabolites, including psychostimulants, fentanyl, prescription opioids, medications for opioid use disorder, xylazine, and THC during the 2025 Super Bowl and Mardi Gras in New Orleans, Louisiana. Raw wastewater (n = 28) was collected during the Super Bowl and Mardi Gras weeks and typical weeks before or after the events. Samples were extracted and analyzed for residual drug residues employing isotopic dilution mass spectrometry using a state-of-the-art ultraperformance liquid chromatography and tandem mass spectrometry technique. The cocaine discharge during Mardi Gras (1220 ± 390 g/d) was significantly higher (p = 0.023) than a typical week. However, fentanyl discharge after Mardi Gras (4.43 ± 1.50 g/d) was significantly higher than during the Mardi Gras week (p = 0.015). This corresponds to an average daily discharge of 3.18 kg of cocaine (31,800 doses), 0.59 kg of methamphetamine (19,600 doses), 0.050 kg of fentanyl (49,600 doses), and 7.03 kg of THC (234,000 doses) during the 2025 Super Bowl and Mardi Gras in New Orleans. Average equivalent consumptions calculated based on estimated populations during the Super Bowl and Mardi Gras weeks, such as cocaine (5380–10,500 mg/d/1000 people), methamphetamine (1200–1780 mg/d/1000 people), and fentanyl (90.6–150 mg/d/1000 people), were not significantly higher than those during baseline weeks. Evidence-based mass loads of substances will be useful for the event planners, safety professionals, and emergency medical service personnel for improved understanding and prediction of spectator behavior to minimize associated public health risk.

item.title: Natural Beeswax-Seed Oil Coatings for Shell Eggs: Effects on Physicochemical, Functional, and Microbiological Quality during Chilled Storage
item.description:
Abstract
Shell eggs lose quality rapidly during storage because the porous shell allows moisture and carbon dioxide to escape, allowing air and bacteria to enter. Beeswax is an effective natural barrier against moisture transfer; however, it possesses limited intrinsic antimicrobial activity. In this study, the effectiveness of beeswax-based coatings enriched with cold-pressed sesame oil or black cumin oil at concentrations of 3% and 5% (w/w) was evaluated for preserving the quality and microbial stability of grade A table eggs during 5 weeks of refrigerated storage at 4 °C. Uncoated, water-washed, and pure beeswax-coated eggs were included as control treatments. Quality attributes were assessed at weekly intervals and included weight loss, air-cell height, Haugh unit, yolk index, shape index, component weights, CIE color parameters, albumen and yolk pH, soluble solids content, foaming capacity, and emulsion stability. Microbiological quality was evaluated by enumerating total aerobic mesophilic bacteria, coliforms, and molds and yeasts. Coating treatment significantly affected weight loss, air-cell height, yolk index, albumen and yolk pH, albumen and yolk color, foaming capacity, emulsion stability, and all microbial counts (P < 0.05), whereas Haugh unit, shape index, shell thickness, and yolk weight were not significantly affected. Storage time and the treatment × time interaction significantly influenced weight loss, air-cell height, color parameters, albumen pH, soluble solids, foaming capacity, emulsion stability, and microbial counts. Beeswax-based coatings reduced weight loss and air-cell expansion and contributed to the preservation of yolk index, while washed eggs exhibited the most rapid deterioration, highlighting the protective function of the natural cuticle. Albumen pH increased during storage; however, this increase was most effectively limited by pure beeswax and beeswax containing 5% black cumin oil, suggesting improved resistance to gas transfer. Washed eggs exhibited the highest microbial loads, reaching 1040 CFU g–1, whereas all beeswax-based coatings, with or without added oil, maintained microbial counts at or near the detection limit throughout storage. Since pure beeswax generally performed comparably to the oil-enriched coatings in controlling microbial growth, the enhanced microbiological stability of coated eggs appears to be primarily associated with physical pore sealing by the wax, while any additional antimicrobial contribution from the incorporated oils should be regarded as a possible complementary mechanism. Overall, beeswax-based coatings, either alone or enriched with sesame or black cumin oil, represent a promising natural strategy for preserving the physical quality and microbiological stability of shell eggs during refrigerated storage.

item.title: Molecular Dynamics Insight into Softening Mechanism of Zirconia and Prediction of Removal Depth in Magnetic Abrasive Finishing
item.description:
Abstract
Zirconia ceramic is widely used in dentistry and precision industries owing to its high hardness and fracture toughness. Nevertheless, its high hardness and toughness cause severe tool wear, and microcracks tend to form on the machined surface during conventional mechanical processing. This paper proposes a NaOH-PVP-deionized water composite system to realize green chemical softening of zirconia at room temperature and atmospheric pressure. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that OH– forms strong chemical bonds with surface Zr atoms, thereby inducing surface hydroxylation and increasing the diffusion coefficient of Zr atoms. Adsorbed PVP molecules further regulate the softening process and transform the material from a rigid to a softened state. Simulations verify that such softening is essentially a corrosion reaction and predict the corrosion depth and corrosion rate within 60 min. Experiments combining chemical softening and magnetic abrasive finishing (MAF) show that the surface roughness of zirconia specimens decreases from Ra 0.302 to 0.057, and the material removal rate ranges from 2.29 × 10–3 μm/s to 2.93 × 10–3 μm/s. The average error between simulated and measured removal depths is only 17.02%. This composite system enables effective surface softening of zirconia. The simulation can reproduce the experimental trend, providing feasible theoretical support and a technical route for high-efficiency, low-damage precision machining of zirconia.

item.title: Computational Structural and Dynamic Insights into the Proposed TcP21–CXCR4 Interaction: A Consensus-Based Multireplica Simulation Approach
item.description:
Abstract
Chagas disease, caused by Trypanosoma cruzi, is a neglected tropical disease with limited therapeutic options, underscoring the need for novel targeted strategies. The parasite’s secreted 21 kDa virulence factor, TcP21, promotes extracellular amastigote host-cell invasion and persistence by interacting with the human chemokine receptor CXCR4, a class A G protein-coupled receptor. Despite its biological importance, the structural determinants governing TcP21–CXCR4 complex formation remain unknown. To elucidate the molecular basis of this host–parasite recognition, multiple initial candidate binding modes were generated via molecular docking using the experimentally resolved active-state CXCR4 structure (PDB ID: 8K3Z) and then subjected to extensive multireplica molecular dynamics (MD) simulations within a biomimetic lipid bilayer. Consensus analyses integrating solvent-accessible surface area (SASA), dynamic contact profiling, and hydrogen bond occupancy across independent conformational ensembles were used to characterize recurrent features of the proposed interface. The results support a structural model in which TcP21 engages CXCR4 through a continuous interaction region localized within the LYS23–PHE39 segment, whereas CXCR4 presents a hierarchically organized and distributed interface. Within this model, a relatively stable interaction core involving the TM5, TM6, and TM7 domains is predominantly characterized by van der Waals contacts, while a more conformationally adaptable peripheral anchoring region involving the ECL2, TM1, and N-terminal domains contributes additional intermolecular interactions. The recurrence of these features across independent simulations supports their consideration as candidate determinants of TcP21–CXCR4 recognition, although their structural and biological relevance remains to be experimentally established. Overall, the resulting computational model provides atomistic structural hypotheses for TcP21–CXCR4 recognition and a basis for future experimental studies to examine the predicted interface and assess its potential relevance to TcP21–CXCR4-mediated interactions.

item.title: Chain Length, Unsaturation, and Conformational State Modulate ω-3 FFA Effects on POPC Bilayers
item.description:
Abstract
Free fatty acids (FFAs), specifically the ω-3 forms α-linolenic acid (ALA), eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA), and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), are important modulators of lipid membrane structure and dynamics, yet how these three species compare within a single, consistent framework remains unclear. Here, we employed atomistic molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the effects of ALA, EPA, and DHA (5–20 mol %) on 1-palmitoyl-2-oleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine (POPC) bilayers in single-FFA and mixed DHA/EPA systems. FFA incorporation induces concentration-dependent bilayer condensation, marked by decreased area and volume per lipid, increased thickness, and enhanced acyl chain order, with ALA producing the strongest effects. All three FFAs promote reorientation of POPC headgroups toward embedded FFA carboxyl groups. Using a conformational classification scheme (stretched, intermediate, coiled), we show that local ordering of neighboring POPC chains and the FFAs’ own ordering strongly depend on conformational state. FFAs exhibit higher lateral mobility than POPC. Passive transbilayer diffusion depends on FFA type and concentration; only ALA is nonmonotonic. In mixed DHA/EPA systems, lateral diffusion of EPA is enhanced relative to single-FFA systems, whereas passive diffusion of DHA is reduced. These results show that chain length and unsaturation mainly modulate FFA effects on bilayer structure and dynamics, whereas conformational state additionally shapes local acyl-chain ordering, relevant to membrane behavior under elevated and pathological FFA levels.

item.title: Structural–Response Consistency Evaluation of a Jiulong Coking Coal Molecular Model Based on Multi-Characterization Constraints
item.description:
Abstract
The evaluation of coal molecular models commonly relies on individual criteria, such as structural parameter matching, density agreement, or consistency in adsorption behavior. However, these indicators are usually considered independently, and a unified quantitative framework for integrating different evaluation dimensions is still lacking. In this study, an average organic molecular model of Jiulong (JL) coking coal was constructed based on ultimate analysis, 13C NMR, FTIR, and XPS characterization, and a structure–response consistency evaluation framework was established by integrating structural constraints and multiresponse analysis. Based on aromatic carbon fraction, XBP, C–O/C═O ratio, and pyrrolic N/pyridinic N ratio, the molecular formula of the JL coal model was determined as C205H144O30N4. Five indices, including the structural constraint consistency index (SCI), density consistency index (DCI), adsorption response consistency index (ACI), dynamic wetting trajectory consistency index (WCI), and multiresponse consistency index (MCVI), were proposed to quantify structural constraint satisfaction and response consistency. The results indicate that the model effectively retains the structural features derived from multicharacterization, with an (SCI) value of 0.981. The simulated density of the aggregate model was 1.22 g/cm3, and the relative deviation from the mineral-corrected equivalent density of the organic framework decreased to 2.24%, corresponding to a (DCI) value of 0.978. The simulated and experimental CO2 adsorption behaviors exhibited a similar overall trend, with an (ACI) value of 0.807. However, deviations were observed around Pc ≈ 0.03 MPa, indicating that the model reasonably describes micropore-dominated adsorption but does not fully represent pore relaxation, mineral–coal interactions, and heterogeneous adsorption sites at relatively higher pressures. Both experimental and simulated contact angles decreased during wetting, yielding a (WCI) value of 0.682, suggesting that interfacial wettability is more sensitive to polar site distribution, surface roughness, and mineral components. The (MCVI) value of 0.862 indicates an overall structure–response consistency of the model, although differences exist among different response dimensions. This study provides a quantitative framework for evaluating the consistency and applicability of coal molecular models.

item.title: Improving LC-MS-Based Marfey’s Analysis on a Single-Quadrupole Platform through Reagent Evaluation and SIM/Scan Acquisition
item.description:
Abstract
Marfey’s method is a widely used approach for determining the absolute configuration of amino acids in peptides and natural products. However, its broader application is often limited by challenges in resolving amino acid epimers and the relatively large amount of analyte typically required for analysis. In this study, we evaluated three commonly used Marfey’s reagents (l-FDAA, l-FDVA, and l-FDLA) for their ability to resolve amino acid diastereomers and investigated whether synchronous selected ion monitoring (SIM)/scan mode in liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (LC-MS) could improve the sensitivity of LC-MS analysis. Using the cyanobacterial peptide micropeptin 982 (d-Gln) as a representative case study, we evaluated three acquisition modes on a widely available single-quadrupole LC-MS platform and found that synchronous SIM/scan, particularly with time-segmented SIM groups, substantially improved practical sensitivity while preserving scan-mode information. Limits of detection were achieved in the range of 11–16 pmol, and absolute configuration assignments were accomplished using as little as 50 μg of analyte. This method provides a practical strategy for stereochemical analysis of scarce peptide natural products, especially when material needs to be prioritized for downstream biological research.

item.title: Exsolution-Engineered Ni-Based Titanate Perovskites for Dry Reforming of Methane: Activity-Stability Trade-Offs and Deactivation Mechanisms
item.description:
Abstract
Syngas production via dry reforming of methane (DRM) represents a promising route for the valorization of carbon-based molecules, CH4 and CO2, in the emerging decarbonization era. However, the harsh operating conditions required by DRM demand highly active and robust catalysts to exploit this process for hydrogen production. In this context, the rational design of thermally stable catalysts with enhanced resistance to deactivation becomes essential. Herein, we focus on elucidating the structural and morphological evolution of Ni-, Ni–Co-, and Ni–Fe-doped titanates with a perovskite framework during guest cation incorporation and subsequent exsolution. Structural, compositional, and surface modifications were investigated by XRD, SEM, EDX, XAFS, N2 physisorption, and XPS. The catalytic performance of the exsolved materials was evaluated in DRM. The Ni-doped titanate (LSTNO-H) exhibited higher catalytic activity than Ni/γ-Al2O3 for CO2 conversion, reaching 80% conversion at 708 °C compared to 715 °C under short-term tests. However, the titanates still show room for improvement in long-term activity and durability. To elucidate the mechanisms governing catalyst deactivation, DRM tests were performed under diluted conditions, enabling a comparative assessment of structural and surface changes during reaction. Under such conditions, catalyst deactivation was mainly associated with nanoparticle sintering, with partial metal oxidation potentially contributing to activity loss, while no significant carbon deposition was detected. In contrast, the benchmark Ni/γ-Al2O3 catalyst showed carbon deposition, although no measurable deactivation occurred under the investigated conditions. Overall, this study highlights the potential of exsolution-based titanates for DRM while providing insights into the deactivation behavior of exsolved Ni under the investigated conditions.

item.title: Simulation of Electron Trapping in Polymer Light-Emitting Diodes
item.description:
Abstract
Electron trapping in polymer light-emitting diodes (PLEDs) operated at constant voltage results in a decrease of current and light emission over many minutes, and the decline becomes more pronounced with decreasing temperature. This seems to contradict the established electron trap formation scenario, which is temperature-activated and therefore decelerates when cooling down. Numerical simulations are performed on the device characteristics of pristine PLEDs and during operation, i.e., when electron traps form. The experimental current and emission trends are explained by a temperature-dependent variation of the trap occupancy, which is determined by the temperature-dependent charge mobilities and capture rates. Matching the simulated electron trap density between the PLED and the electron-only device requires a very slow electron capture rate, which is reasoned by the specific electron trap formation process in semiconducting polymers.

item.title: The Chemical Arsenal of Amazonian Tree Frogs: Evolutionary Diversification of Skin Peptides across Phyllomedusidae
item.description:
Abstract
Amphibian poisons are one of the most complex chemical defense systems among vertebrates, yet their diversity remains largely unresolved. Here, we present a comparative peptidomic analysis of six Amazonian species of Monkey Tree Frogs (Phyllomedusidae) sampled across three geographic regions. Mass spectrometry-based profiling revealed 18,466 features. Despite this extensive diversity, a subset of 961 features was shared across all species, while thousands of additional features were restricted to individual taxa or combinations of taxa. Poison profiles showed a highly uneven relative abundance distribution, with a small number of peptides accounting for a large proportion of the detected signal. Phylloseptins and dermaseptins were prominent components of several profiles, whereas bradykinin-related peptides, tryptophyllins, dermorphin-like peptides, medusins, and phyllomedusins showed variable contributions across taxa and regions. Geographic variation in the relative abundance of major peptide subfamilies indicates differences in peptide composition among the sampled populations. Such patterns are consistent with spatially structured variation and align with previous studies suggesting that amphibian peptide repertoires may be shaped by local ecological and biotic interactions. Our results reveal substantial variation in peptide composition and relative abundance while maintaining a broadly shared molecular component across phyllomedusid taxa. This study expands current knowledge of amphibian chemical diversity and provides new insights into how ecological and evolutionary processes may contribute to the diversification of chemical defense systems.

item.title: StructRSMA: A Proof-of-Concept Framework for PDB-Derived Contact-Supervised Transfer in RNA-Small Molecule Binding Affinity Prediction
item.description:
Abstract
RNA-small molecule affinity data sets usually provide only pair-level labels, making it difficult for multiview models to learn local nucleotide-atom recognition patterns. We present StructRSMA, a proof-of-concept contact-supervised transfer framework built on the DeepRSMA backbone. StructRSMA preserves the RNA sequence, RNA graph, molecule sequence, molecule graph, cross-fusion, and base affinity components, while introducing PDB-derived nucleotide-atom contact supervision and a Structural Contact Adapter (SCA). In Stage 1, RNA-ligand complexes are converted into binary contact maps using a 4 Å cutoff, and the shared backbone and contact head are trained to rank local contacts. In Stage 2, the contact-pretrained parameters are transferred to R-SIM, where only pKd labels are used; the frozen contact head supplies inferred contact priors to SCA for residual affinity calibration. Under a fixed validation-selected independent-test protocol, the reproduced DeepRSMA baseline obtained PCC 0.387 ± 0.022 and RMSE 0.970 ± 0.012. Contact500 pretraining without SCA yielded PCC 0.418 ± 0.048 and RMSE 0.951 ± 0.023, whereas full StructRSMA reached PCC 0.441 ± 0.037 and RMSE 0.918 ± 0.020. No-pretraining, shuffled-contact, and parameter-matched adapter controls did not reproduce the full improvement. Feature-removal and view-randomization analyses further indicated that contact statistics and multiview context contribute jointly to SCA. Contact prediction showed probability enrichment above contact density, but weak thresholded classification, and improvements became smaller and statistically uncertain under deoverlapped and cold evaluations. StructRSMA therefore provides evidence that PDB-derived contact supervision can support affinity calibration under covered data distributions, while explicitly identifying the limits of structural transfer.

item.title: Optically Controlled Hybrid Metasurface for Efficient Terahertz Frequency Modulation
item.description:
Abstract
Terahertz waves exhibit considerable application value in fields such as high-speed wireless communication, nondestructive testing, and biomedical imaging owing to their broadband transmission and low photon energy characteristics. However, existing hybrid metasurfaces integrated with active materials suffer from the inherent electromagnetic response of the structure and limited reconfigurability, making broadband frequency modulation difficult to achieve. To address these challenges, this work proposes a terahertz metasurface frequency modulation device based on a composite structure of double-opening square split-rings and metal patches, and systematically investigates how the geometric parameters and the incidence angle govern the resonance characteristics. Numerical simulations show that adjusting the structural parameters and incidence angle can produce significant resonant frequency shifts and enable flexible modulation of the number and distribution of resonant peaks. On this basis, two germanium-based optically controlled hybrid metasurface schemes are further proposed. By embedding germanium in the key structural regions, dynamic frequency regulation is numerically demonstrated under optical pumping, with a maximum tuning range of 0.8 THz, exhibiting excellent dynamic modulation performance. The proposed metasurface combines the advantages of static regulation and active modulation, offering a new insight into efficient dynamic manipulation of terahertz waves and holding great promise for high-speed wireless communication and high-sensitivity biosensing.

item.title: Rigorous Benchmarking of Continuous Dry-Printed CNT Networks as High-Performance Electrochemical Sensors
item.description:
Abstract
In this study, we present a systematic evaluation of the electrochemical performance of floating catalyst chemical vapor deposited carbon nanotubes (FCCVD-CNTs) and compare their performance against conventional carbon, gold, and platinum electrodes. Differential pulse voltammetry and cyclic voltammetry were employed to detect well-established benchmark redox species, such as methylene blue, 3,3′,5,5′-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB), and acetaminophen (commonly known as paracetamol), in both buffer and human plasma, serving as proof-of-concept for the proposed approach. The FCCVD-CNTs achieved superior electrochemical sensor performance metrics, such as their signal-to-noise ratio, signal-to-background ratio, and detection limit, highlighting their potential as a novel material to redefine sensing standards in complex biological environments. Recognizing the challenges associated with processing an electrode material into a scalable, robust, high-performance, ready-to-use platform, particularly in the form of a miniaturized electrochemical cell such as a screen-printed electrode (SPE), we benchmarked our FCCVD-CNT-based dry-printed electrode (DPE) against commercially available, ink processed SPEs to assess its practical suitability for biosensing applications. The obtained results corroborate the capability of the CNT DPEs as a robust alternative for biosensing applications in a clinically representative matrix.

item.title: Hyperspectral Soil Metal Estimation Using Fractional-Order Derivatives and LSTM–KAN Modeling
item.description:
Abstract
Hyperspectral estimation of soil heavy metals is challenging because their spectral responses are weak, indirect, and strongly affected by the soil matrix. In this study, 167 surface soil samples collected from a karst open-pit coal mining area in Guizhou, China, were analyzed for As, Cr, Cu, and Hg. Spectra were processed using fractional-order derivative (FOD) preprocessing over orders of 0.0–2.0 and reorganized into wavelength-ordered sequences for a long short-term memory network coupled with a Kolmogorov–Arnold network regression head (LSTM–KAN). Random forest (RF), partial least-squares regression (PLSR), and LSTM with a fully connected regression head (LSTM–FC) were used for comparison. Using the same 117/50 sample-level holdout split across all models and elements, LSTM–KAN achieved the best overall validation performance, with a mean R2 of 0.9692 across the four metals. The holdout-selected FOD orders were 1.2 for As and Hg, 1.8 for Cr, and 1.4 for Cu. 10-fold cross-validation further supported the internal consistency of LSTM–KAN, yielding overall R2 values of 0.9148–0.9879. Spectral regions showing strong metal–reflectance correlations were mainly concentrated around 2200–2300 nm, while the FOD orders maximizing spectral correlation differed from those producing the best predictive performance. These results demonstrate that combining FOD preprocessing with wavelength-ordered sequence modeling can improve quantitative estimation of soil heavy metals within the Jinsha study area data set.

item.title: Theoretical Calculations of CO 2 /CH 4 Separation through Windowed Carbon Nanotube Membranes
item.description:
Abstract
Distinct topological features endow windowed carbon nanotube (CNT) membranes with great potential as molecular sieves for efficient gas separation and purification. In this work, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were adopted to systematically investigate the CO2/CH4 selective separation performance of such membranes. Key structural and operational parameters, including CNT diameter, pressure, initial feed gas molar ratio, and nanowindow density, were modulated to comprehensively evaluate the molecular sieving capacity toward CO2 and CH4. Simulation results reveal that heteroatom-functionalized windowed CNT membranes exhibit outstanding CO2 permselectivity and superior CH4 purification capacity, with a maximum CO2/CH4 separation selectivity of 41. Among all simulated configurations, the 4N5F-modified nanowindow CNT membrane exhibits the optimal separation performance, yielding a CO2 capture fraction of 0.77 and recovered CH4 purity of 97.6%. Such excellent molecular sieving performance confirms that windowed CNT membranes hold promising prospects for direct CO2 capture and raw shale gas purification.

item.title: Novel Aeschynite-Type CeTiTa 1– x Nb x O 6 Orange Pigments
item.description:
Abstract
An orange inorganic pigment free from hazardous components conventionally used in inorganic pigments, such as Cd-, Pb-, Hg-, and Cr(VI)-based compounds, was developed based on aeschynite-type CeTiTa1–xNbxO6 (0 ≤ x ≤ 1) synthesized by a solid-state reaction method. X-ray powder diffraction, Rietveld refinement, and X-ray fluorescence analysis supported the formation of a continuous CeTiTa1–xNbxO6 solid solution over the investigated composition range, with a small amount of TiO2 impurity. UV–visible reflectance spectroscopy showed that increasing Nb5+ substitution shifted the absorption edge toward longer wavelengths, while the optical band gap energy estimated from Tauc plots decreased from 2.45 to 2.12 eV. This behavior may be associated with modification of the transition-metal d-derived conduction-band states upon Nb substitution. As a result, the sample color gradually changed from yellow to orange with increasing Nb content, and CeTiNbO6 (x = 1) exhibited a high redness value (a* = +26.4). X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy indicated that Ce3+ was the predominant Ce species in the surface region probed by XPS. CeTiNbO6 retained its orange coloration after the acid and base treatments employed in this study and after heat treatment at 800 °C for 6 h in air. These results indicate that CeTiTa1–xNbxO6 is a promising orange inorganic pigment with composition-tunable color and good color stability under the chemical and thermal conditions examined in this study.

item.title: Microbubble-Assisted Bioresorbable Biphasic Scaffolds Reinforced with TiO 2 Nanosheets for Oral and Maxillofacial Bone Repair: In Vitro Evaluation
item.description:
Abstract
This study presents the development of bioresorbable biphasic scaffolds incorporating titanium dioxide (TiO2) nanostructures, specifically nanoparticles (TNPs) and nanosheets (TNSs), into a poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) and silk fibroin (SF) polymeric matrix using a bubbling technique followed by freeze-drying. Both TNPs and TNSs were synthesized via a hydrothermal method. The resulting scaffolds featured two distinct layers: a porous sponge-like structure and a dense film, designed to mimic the architecture of natural bone and soft tissue interfaces in oral and maxillofacial regions. Structural characterization confirmed the successful integration of TiO2 nanostructures within the scaffold matrix. X-ray diffraction showed that both TNPs and TNSs exhibited a pure anatase phase. Compared to TNPs, the nanosheet form offered significantly improved molecular mobility and dispersion within the matrix. Additionally, TNSs-incorporated scaffolds exhibited favorable porosity, compressive strength, swelling behavior, and degradation rate. In vitro studies demonstrated enhanced proliferation of both osteoblasts and fibroblasts, particularly in the TNSs scaffolds. The anatase-phase TiO2 contributed to improved cell-material interactions and scaffold performance without significant cytotoxicity. These findings suggest that TNSs-based scaffolds hold strong potential as functional biomaterials for oral and maxillofacial tissue repair, including alveolar cleft and mandibular ridge reconstruction.

item.title: Pharmaceutical Salt Formation as a Strategy to Enhance In Situ Drug Loading into Apatite-Based Materials
item.description:
Abstract
Water-based loading is attractive for pharmaceutical and industrial applications and helps prevent damage to drug carriers; however, the poor aqueous solubility of many APIs, such as ciprofloxacin (CIP), limits their incorporation into these systems. To overcome these limitations, this work explores the use of a ciprofloxacin–dexketoprofen (CIP–DKT) pharmaceutical salt to improve API solubility and in situ loading into sensitive apatite platforms, including biomimetic apatite nanoparticles (Ap) and apatite-mineralized eggshell membranes (ApESM). Computational and solid-state characterization rationalized the improved aqueous solubility and drug loading observed with CIP–DKT. CIP showed higher affinity for the negatively charged apatite surface, whereas DKT displayed lower affinity and, due to its acidic nature, altered the synthesis pH, affecting apatite morphology and ESM mineralization. Interestingly, CIP–DKT enabled the simultaneous incorporation of CIP and DKT while preserving the biomimetic apatite morphology and the mineralization of the ESMs, likely due to the buffering effect of CIP. Final HPLC and antibacterial assays confirmed pH-dependent API release and sustained antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli, with improved diffusion from ApESM–CIP–DKT. Overall, these results demonstrate that pharmaceutical salt formation is an efficient strategy to enhance the incorporation of poorly soluble APIs into sensitive materials under water-based processing conditions.

item.title: Photoconversion Behavior of a ZnO/Graphite Solar Cell
item.description:
Abstract
This work assembled dye solar cells by replacing platinum with graphite on indium tin oxide (ITO). First, the device was tested only on the ITO; afterward, graphite was placed on the ITO and evaluated as a counter electrode in the cell. The results showed that the presence of graphite increased the incident photocurrent conversion (IPCE) of the cell. The electrode used was a combination of zinc oxide with 4% bismuth, and characterization of the film had high reflectance in the visible region, a thickness of around 1.47 μm, and a crystallite size of around 38.5 nm. The addition of graphite as a counter electrode increased the cell efficiency by 10 times, driven by an increase in current density from 0.02 to 1.2 mA/cm and in IPCE from 0.04 to 2.26%.

item.title: Ti-Based Template Incorporated with RGD Amino Motif as a Domain Supporting Self-Assembly of Extracellular Matrix in Bone Tissue Regeneration: Preparation, Characterization, and Correlated Structure to Identified Application
item.description:
Abstract
Bone tissue engineering utilizing bioactive materials represents a promising strategy for regenerating bone defects and stimulating new tissue growth. In this study, a biocompatible, bone-mimicking material was developed by incorporating the arginine–glycine–aspartate (RGD) amino motif onto the surface of a titanium-based metal–organic framework (MOF), MIL-125, using a simple solvent-soaking method to impart osteoinductive properties. The molecular incorporation, phase composition, and surface morphology of the functionalized MIL-125 powder were comprehensively characterized using microdifferential scanning calorimetry (Micro-DSC), XRD, SEM, EDX, and FT-IR. Among the investigated conditions, the MIL-125 sample prepared with 0.25 mg of RGD and a 36 h soaking time exhibited the most favorable physicochemical characteristics based on the combined structural, spectroscopic, thermal, elemental, and morphological analyses. SEM analysis revealed the initial development of needle-like RGD-associated structures at 0.15 mg of RGD, which was consistent with the appearance of an exothermic Micro-DSC peak associated with RGD interaction with the MIL-125 surface. Furthermore, quantum chemical calculations were performed to elucidate the molecular-level interaction mechanisms between the peptide and the MOF framework. The computational results uncovered two stable adsorption configurations within the MIL-125 pore structure. Among these, the aspartic acid (ASP)-terminal-coordinated titanium oxide cluster of MIL-125 exhibited the highest thermodynamic stability, possessing an adsorption energy of −24.99 kcal/mol, which was more than 2-fold stronger than the arginine (ARG)-terminal interaction. This strong electronic binding corroborates the experimentally observed RGD immobilization. Ultimately, these fundamental insights into RGD–MOF chemical interactions provide a robust framework for developing advanced bioactive components suitable for orthopedic regeneration applications.

item.title: Phosphorescent Sensing of ADN Using Copper(I) Coordination Polymers
item.description:
Abstract
Rapid, selective, and field-deployable detection of ammonium dinitramide (ADN) is important for the safe production, handling, and monitoring of energetic materials. Herein, we report a distinct synthetic strategy for the known Cu(I) coordination polymer [Cu(pz)]n and reveal its previously unexplored phosphorescent sensing capability toward ADN. Inspired by the thermal reduction of related Cu(II) imidazolate frameworks, Pbca-[Cu(pz)]n was prepared from Cu(pz)2 via high-temperature reduction and vapor deposition, affording diffraction-quality single crystals for accurate structural refinement and photophysical analysis. To the best of our knowledge, this work represents the first application of [Cu(pz)]n as a phosphorescent sensing platform for ADN. Upon exposure to ADN, [Cu(pz)]n shows phosphorescence quenching mainly via competitive absorption (CA), with possible photoinduced electron transfer (PET) contribution. The Stern–Volmer response shows a linear relationship over the ADN concentration range of 0–80 μM (R2 = 0.987), with a Stern–Volmer constant (KSV) of 2.7 × 104 M–1 and a detection limit of 5.56 μM. Although previously reported graphene-based voltammetric and AuNP-based colorimetric methods achieve lower detection limits of 2.0 μM and approximately 0.10 μM, respectively, they rely on electrode-based measurements or multistep UV-assisted chemical conversion and derivatization. In contrast, [Cu(pz)]n enables direct phosphorescence sensing of ADN without such pretreatment and shows high selectivity over the tested energetic materials. Furthermore, [Cu(pz)]n can be incorporated into test strips for visual ADN detection, demonstrating its potential as a simple and convenient platform for rapid on-site screening.

item.title: Forced Ignition of NH 3 /H 2 Blends in a Mixing Layer with Different Air Temperatures
item.description:
Abstract
Hydrogen addition has attracted significant attention due to its ability to improve the combustion performance of ammonia. However, the forced ignition mechanism of ammonia blended with hydrogen with various air temperatures under nonpremixed conditions remains unclear at present. The forced ignition process of ammonia-hydrogen blended fuel in a mixing layer is systematically investigated using numerical simulations. Three air temperatures, TO = 450, 750, and 1050 K, are considered. The results show that for the cases with TO = 450 and 750 K, a tetrabrachial flame structure, consisting of two premixed branches and two nonpremixed branches, forms in the mixing layer after ignition. The flame is dominated by a propagating mode. When the air temperature is increased to 1050 K, the edge flame initially exhibits a tetrabrachial flame structure dominated by propagation, but later an autoignition-dominated branch appears upstream, resulting in a pentabrachial flame structure. The OH transport-budget analysis indicates that the autoignition branch is dominated by chemical reactions, with diffusion playing a comparatively minor role. In addition, HO2 and H2O2 serve as key markers for the formation of an autoignition branch. Analysis of the chemical reactions in the different flame branches shows that heat release in the lean nonpremixed branch is dominated by the hydrogen oxidation reaction system, while the rich nonpremixed branch is controlled by ammonia oxidation and nitrogen chemical reaction pathways. The reactions in the autoignition branch are primarily associated with the hydrogen–oxygen chain reactions. The thermal contributions of each branch further indicate that the premixed branch is the primary source of heat release for the edge flame. Increasing the air temperature not only enhances the heat release intensity of each propagation branch, but also activates the thermal contribution of the autoignition flame branch.

item.title: Experimental Research on Two-Phase Pulse Detonation Characteristics under Elevated Initial Pressures and High-Frequency Conditions
item.description:
Abstract
To investigate the operating characteristics of two-phase pulse detonation engines (PDEs) under elevated initial pressures and high-frequency conditions, experiments were conducted using gasoline as the fuel and 50% oxygen-enriched air as the oxidizer. Elevated initial pressures ranging from 0.10 to 0.31 MPa have been achieved by increasing the reactant supply pressures and installing convergent nozzles with varying contraction ratios at the tube exit. The results show that, as the supply pressure increases, the stable detonation ranges both the equivalence ratio and the oxidizer-to-fuel supply pressure ratio initially widen and then narrow. All stable detonation cycles occur at supply pressure ratios below unity. Increasing the initial pressure enables stable detonation under fuel-lean conditions, with the lowest equivalence ratios decreasing to 0.495 and 0.492 for contraction ratios of 1.23 and 1.0, respectively. The nozzle with a contraction ratio of 1.56 provides the widest equivalence ratio range, spanning from 0.811 to 2.530. Moreover, increasing the initial pressure has only a limited influence on the deflagration-to-detonation transition (DDT) distance in the present study. The detonation wave pressure increases almost linearly with rising initial pressure, reaching a detonation-to-initial pressure ratio of 29.85. Furthermore, the maximum stable detonation frequency depends on both the nozzle contraction ratio and the initial pressure. A stable frequency of 100 Hz is achieved under specific initial pressure and contraction ratio conditions, while excessively large contraction ratios or significant increases in initial pressure can reduce the stable operating frequency.

item.title: Diagenetic Evolution of Deep Tight Sandstone Reservoirs in the Lower Jurassic Strata of the Kuqa Depression, Tarim Basin
item.description:
Abstract
Deep sandstone reservoirs are generally characterized by low permeability; nevertheless, effective reservoir rocks can still develop within them. However, the types of effective reservoir rocks and tight rocks require further characterization, and the differences in their diagenetic processes warrant further investigation. This study examines the diagenetic evolutionary processes of different petrofacies in the tight sandstone reservoirs of the Jurassic Ahe Formation in the Kuqa Depression of the Tarim Basin, based on analyses of effective reservoir rocks and tight petrofacies. Research indicates that the sandstones of the Jurassic Ahe Formation are predominantly medium- to coarse-grained lithic sandstones with minor feldspathic litharenite. These sandstones are classified into three petrofacies: petrofacies A (ductile lithic-lean sandstone), petrofacies B (ductile lithic-rich sandstone), and petrofacies C (tightly carbonate-cemented sandstone). These three petrofacies exhibit significant differences in terms of diagenesis and diagenetic pathways. Petrofacies A is an effective reservoir rock, characterized by a relatively high content of rigid grains. During burial, fluid activity was frequent, causing this petrofacies to experience multiple episodes and types of diagenesis. Cement types are diverse but occur in low abundance, and secondary dissolution pores are relatively well developed. Petrofacies B and C are classified as tight petrofacies. Petrofacies B contains a high abundance of ductile grains; during the early diagenetic stage, severe porosity loss occurs because of mechanical compaction. Late diagenesis is dominated by clay mineral transformation, with almost no other fluid–rock interactions occurring. Similarly, petrofacies C experiences extensive pore filling by calcite cements during early diagenesis, making pore spaces exceptionally rare and leading to weak fluid–rock interactions. This study contributes to the analysis of deep tight sandstone reservoir quality and the identification of effective reservoir rocks capable of hosting hydrocarbon accumulation, thereby providing a geological basis for deep hydrocarbon exploration and development.

item.title: Quantitative Toxicophore Discovery through Interpretable Deep Learning: A Framework for Mechanism-Guided Toxicity Mitigation in Drug Safety Profiling
item.description:
Abstract
Unanticipated toxicity accounts for ∼30% of clinical-phase drug failures, yet despite advances in computational toxicity prediction, predictive models typically offer scores without identifying the structural culprit. Here, we introduce an interpretable deep-learning framework that couples fingerprint-descriptor fusion with task-adaptive attention and a SHAP-guided bioisosteric ablation pipeline. Trained on 9,315 compounds spanning 14 end points (Tox21 + ClinTox) under scaffold-stratified split, the attention-fusion model achieves mean test ROC-AUC of 0.739 (Tox21) and 0.953 (ClinTox). The critical advance is a structure-guided validation protocol: predictive intervention ablation─computationally replacing toxicophores with bioisosteric equivalents─demonstrates that the model’s predictions are predictively dependent on specific substructures. Halogen → methyl substitution drops predicted toxicity from 0.659 to 0.101 (paired t = 22.66, p = 6.32 × 10–10, n = 11; Cohen’s d = 6.82), providing the primary structure-guided evidence. Cross-end point SHAP correlation reaches 0.333 (MTL) and 0.334 (STL; Welch’s p = 0.82), indicating that both paradigms extract coherent mechanistic structure above the label baseline (0.172). SMARTS-based toxicophore alignment identifies a strong positive logit differential for aniline on the clinically relevant CT_TOX end point (+0.76), and predictive-intervention ablation confirms model dependence on the identified substructures (halogen → methyl: n = 11, p < 10–9; aniline → methoxy: n = 2, directional check only). External validation on 1,427 SIDER adverse-drug-reaction compounds reveals significant toxicophore enrichment (aniline: 12.6% vs 0%, Fisher exact p = 4.5 × 10–12; halogenated aromatic: 29.8% vs 0%, p = 1.6 × 10–29), remaining significant after controlling for molecular weight and Log P. Three case studies illustrate how SHAP-guided attribution translates into actionable medicinal-chemistry mitigation strategies.

item.title: Outward and Inward Electron Transfer Occur through Distinct Interfacial Electron Transfer Mechanisms for Anaerobic Shewanella oneidensis
item.description:
Abstract
Microbial electrosynthesis (MES) is an emerging biotechnology with the potential to mitigate climate change by recycling carbon dioxide into organic compounds using sustainably generated electricity as the energy source. MES utilizes bacteria as catalysts to transfer electrons from a cathode to a target electron acceptor, such as CO2. For MES to decrease net carbon emissions on a meaningful scale, the rate of inward electron transfer (ET) from the cathode to bacteria must increase. In this work, we investigate this challenge using Shewanella oneidensis, a model metal-reducing bacterium with an extensively studied extracellular electron transfer pathway. The primary ET mechanism for S. oneidensis is the Mtr pathway, a cytochrome c-rich pathway that connects the respiratory electron transport chain to the outer surface of the cell. While the Mtr pathway in S. oneidensis is bidirectional, the magnitude of outward ET (its native respiratory direction) consistently exceeds inward ET, the direction required for MES applications. Here, we present the first direct comparison of ET for both directions using potentiometric techniques. Through chronoamperometry and turnover cyclic voltammetry, we demonstrate that the ET mechanism is direction-dependent. Specifically, we observed distinct roles for supplemental riboflavin, where inward ET from a cathode was dependent on supplemental riboflavin, but outward ET to an anode was not.

item.title: Visible-Light-Driven Photoreduction of Industrial-Grade Graphene Oxide into Single-/Few-Layer Reduced Graphene Oxide Nanosheets: Structural Evolution and Enhanced Electrochemical Energy-Storage Performance
item.description:
Abstract
Graphene oxide (GO)-derived reduced graphene oxide (rGO) is an important two-dimensional carbon material for electrochemical energy storage, yet the controllable conversion of low-cost industrial-grade GO into high-quality rGO remains challenging because of its severe aggregation, multilayer stacking, and heterogeneous oxygen-containing functional groups, which usually require harsh reaction conditions and strong reducing agents. Herein, a mild visible-light-driven photoreduction strategy was exploited to convert industrial-grade GO into single-/few-layer rGO nanosheets under ambient temperature and pressure, using eosin Y as the photosensitizer and triethylamine as the sacrificial electron donor. Most importantly, the time-dependent structural evolution of industrial-grade GO during photoreduction was systematically revealed. Morphological and structural characterizations showed that visible-light irradiation progressively weakened interlayer interactions, promoted the delamination and flattening of stacked GO aggregates, and produced single-/few-layer rGO nanosheets. XRD, FTIR, XPS, Raman, and thermal analyses demonstrated a general decrease in oxygenated carbon species, defect reconstruction, and partial restoration of the sp2-conjugated carbon network. After 180 min, the C/O atomic ratio increased from 2.53 to 6.16 and the BET surface area increased from 325.87 to 472.40 m2 g–1, confirming substantial deoxygenation together with increased accessible surface area. The optimized rGO-3 sample delivered a specific capacitance of 370 F g–1 at 20 mV s–1 in 0.1 M KCl, which is competitive with previously reported rGO-based electrodes evaluated at the same scan rate. After 5000 galvanostatic charge–discharge cycles, rGO-3 retained 92.3% of its initial capacitance with a Coulombic efficiency of 99.4%. EIS measurements in ferro/ferricyanide-containing electrolyte and photocurrent measurements of the final washed rGO electrode further indicated faster interfacial electron transfer toward the redox probe and improved carrier-transport behavior, respectively. This work provides a green and controllable route for converting industrial-grade GO into single-/few-layer rGO nanosheets and clarifies the structural evolution underlying the enhanced electrochemical performance of photoreduced graphene materials.

item.title: Biodegradation and Photodegradation of Mg, Ca, Zn, and Cu Complexes of Biodegradable Chelating Agents (EDDS, HIDS, MGDA, and GLDA)
item.description:
Abstract
The environmental fate of biodegradable aminopolycarboxylate chelating agents is strongly influenced by metal complexation; however, the combined effects of central metal ions and ligand structure on degradation behavior remain insufficiently understood. In this study, the biodegradation and photodegradation of the Mg, Ca, Zn, and Cu complexes of four biodegradable chelating agents (EDDS, HIDS, MGDA, and GLDA) were investigated under activated sludge and UV-lamp irradiation conditions. Biodegradation tests revealed metal-dependent behavior: complexes with the alkaline earth metals Mg and Ca were readily degraded, whereas complexes with the transition metals Zn and Cu, except for the EDDS complexes, exhibited high persistence. A qualitative inverse relationship was observed between biodegradability and metal–ligand stability. In contrast, photodegradation exhibited a distinct metal-specific pattern: Cu complexes underwent photodegradation, whereas Mg, Ca, and Zn complexes showed limited photodegradation regardless of ligand identity. These results demonstrate that the degradability of metal–chelate complexes cannot be predicted solely from the behavior of the corresponding free ligands and highlight the importance of considering metal complexation when evaluating the environmental persistence of biodegradable chelating agents in metal-containing aquatic systems.

item.title: Neutral-pH pNZ Removal Enables Fully Aqueous Solid-Phase Synthesis of Linear and ε-Lys-Branched Peptides
item.description:
Abstract
Aiming to emulate Nature by synthesizing peptides in water, we report pH ∼ 7 Na2S2O4/DIEA-induced pNZ removals as a means of enabling fully aqueous solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS). Furthermore, pNZ removal in water was applied to SPPS of ε-Lys-branched peptides and hybrid pNZ/Fmoc SPPS. Finally, combining our methods for SPPS in water with TFA-free resin cleavages opens the door to fully aqueous, PFAS-free approaches to a variety of complex peptides.

item.title: Tailoring Alginate Encapsulates for Agricultural Biostimulants
item.description:
Abstract
Alginate hydrogels have attracted considerable interest as carriers for agricultural biofertilizers due to their ability to protect and retain bioactive compounds. In this study, alginate encapsulates containing tomato green pomace and liquid fractions of fermented Ascophyllum nodosum were produced by ionic gelation and characterized using rheological, osmometric, and swelling analyses. The influence of alginate concentration, biofertilizer type, fermentation duration, and suspending medium on encapsulate behavior was investigated. All formulations exhibited shear-thinning behavior, while the incorporation of powdered tomato pomace and liquid fractions of fermented seaweed promoted stronger structural interactions within the silica fume suspending medium, resulting in higher viscosities than the corresponding unloaded encapsulates. The extended fermentation of A. nodosum further modified the physicochemical properties of the formulations and increased their resistance to flow. Although alginate encapsulates exhibited similar osmotic properties, swelling measurements revealed differences in network density and cross-linking, highlighting the dominant role of hydrogel architecture in determining encapsulate performance. These findings advance current knowledge on alginate-based encapsulation of agricultural biofertilizers and support the rational design of hydrogel carriers with tailored hydration, transport, and mechanical properties for agricultural applications.

item.title: Recent Advances in Polymeric Hydrogel Materials for Fat, Oil, and Grease Mitigation in Sewer Systems
item.description:
Abstract
Fat, oil, and grease (FOG) accumulation in sewer systems is a major environmental and operational challenge, leading to sewer blockages, reduced hydraulic capacity, increased maintenance costs, and the formation of persistent deposits known as fatbergs. These deposits arise from complex physicochemical processes involving the hydrolysis of triglycerides into free fatty acids, followed by their reaction with divalent metal ions, particularly calcium (Ca2+) and magnesium (Mg2+), resulting in insoluble metallic soaps. Hydrogels comprise a diverse class of three-dimensional hydrated materials, including polymeric and supramolecular systems. In this Review, we specifically focus on polymeric hydrogel-based materials because their tunable network structures, porosity, and surface functionalities may facilitate interactions with lipid-rich contaminants and provide potential platforms for FOG mitigation. The incorporation of ZnO nanomaterials, including poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA)- and polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP)-capped ZnO nanomaterials, into polymeric hydrogel matrices may modify adsorption behaviorand improve mechanical strength, structural stability, and multifunctionality. The discussion covers FOG formation mechanisms, hydrogel-mediated interactions, and advantages and limitations of current FOG management technologies. Particular emphasis is placed on natural-polymer-based hydrogels, highlighting their structural characteristics, adsorption mechanisms, and mitigation performance. However, direct evidence for hydrogel-based materials in established sewer FOG deposits remains limited, with much of the available evidence being derived from related oil-removal studies. Furthermore, the Review highlights key challenges associated with the scalability, long-term stability, regeneration, and potential applications of hydrogel-based materials while outlining future research directions for their rational design, performance evaluation, and eventual translation to practical sewer applications.

item.title: Computational and Experimental Studies of PSMA-Targeted Conjugates Designed for Subcellular Delivery of Theranostic Radiometals to Prostate Cancer Cells
item.description:
Abstract
Background: The membrane receptor prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) is a validated target for theranostic radioconjugates in the treatment and imaging of prostate cancer (PCa). Radioconjugates targeted at PSMA rely mostly on the peptidomimetic glutamate–urea–lysine (Glu–urea–Lys) binding motif to facilitate tumor accumulation. The combination of this binding motif with subcellular targeting moieties, such as acridine orange (AO) and triphenylphosphonium (TPP) derivatives, for nuclear and mitochondrial delivery, respectively, might open the way to innovative dual-target approaches. This study integrated molecular docking, long-timescale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and in vitro PSMA inhibition assays to assess whether the incorporation of AO or TPP disrupts the canonical PSMA binding in DOTA-based conjugates containing the Glu–urea–Lys binding motif designed by our group. Results: Docking analyses indicated that our PSMA-targeted conjugates carrying AO or TPP moieties adopt poses analogous to those of PSMA’s natural substrate N-acetyl-aspartyl-glutamate (NAAG) and of the reference conjugate natIn-PSMA-617, preserving crucial interactions within the arginine-rich S1 pocket and within the glutamate-sensing S1′ pocket. In contrast, their congeners lacking the Glu–urea–Lys binding motif exhibited surface-associated binding but failed to engage stably within the active site of PSMA. MD simulations confirmed the structural stability of the PSMA-conjugate complexes. In vitro inhibition assays supported these observations: the non-PSMA-targeted natIn-AO and natIn-TPP displayed negligible inhibitory activity against PSMA (with noncalculable IC50 values), whereas the dual-target conjugates displayed potency in the submicromolar range. Conclusion: Collectively, our results show that the dual-target conjugates recognize the PSMA protein, with subcellular targeting motifs influencing peripheral dynamics, but not core binding. This framework supports the rational design of multifunctional PSMA-directed radioconjugates for improved subcellular delivery of theranostic radionuclides toward alternative In PCa imaging and management.

item.title: Retraction of “Characterization and Evaluation of Silk Sericin-Based Hydrogel: A Promising Biomaterial for Efficient Healing of Acute Wounds”
item.description: The authors retract this article (DOI: 10.1021/acsomega.3c04178), published in ACS Omega in 2023, 8 (35), 32090–32098, due to concerns identified by authors in Figures 1 and 3 that could not be resolved and that affect the final conclusions of the article.

item.title: Coupled Evolution and Mechanism of Pore Structure and Thermal Maturity in Alkaline Lacustrine Dolomitic Shale
item.description:
Abstract
Alkaline lacustrine shale oil is a critical type of unconventional hydrocarbon resource. However, systematic insights into the coupled evolution between multiscale pore structure and thermal maturity in alkaline lacustrine dolomitic shale are still inadequate, limiting effective exploitation of this resource. Therefore, this study investigates the coupled evolution of thermal maturity and multiscale pore structure in alkaline lacustrine dolomitic shale from the Lower Ganchaigou Formation in the Qaidam Basin. Combining semiclosed pyrolysis simulation with multiple pore characterization techniques, we elucidate the evolutionary patterns and controlling factors of pore structure during thermal maturation. Results reveal that pore volume and specific surface area increase significantly with increasing Ro, accompanied by an overall shift toward larger pore sizes. The volumes of all pore types increase progressively, and differences among their volumes dominate pore heterogeneity. Pore heterogeneity and connectivity exhibit distinct stage-dependent variations. At low maturity (Ro < 0.63%), heavy hydrocarbon filling blocks pore throats and reduces pore space. Within the favorable mature stage (0.63%–1.32% Ro), organic acid dissolution effectively enlarges carbonate mineral pores and boosts macropore development. At the high- to overmaturity stage (Ro > 1.32%), hydrocarbon transformation improves pore connectivity, while mineral recrystallization and compaction homogenize pore distribution and weaken heterogeneity. The maturity interval of 0.63%–1.32% is confirmed as the optimal golden window for reservoir space and retained oil coenrichment. This finding offers quantitative references for pore evolution research and practical guidance for the prediction of favorable shale oil areas in alkaline lacustrine shale sequences.

item.title: Host–Guest Encapsulation of Fullerenes by Lys-2Gly Dendrimers: Physicochemical Characterization and In Vitro Cytotoxicity Evaluations
item.description:
Abstract
We investigate the physicochemical properties of complexes formed between the peptide Lys-2Gly dendrimer and C60 and C70 fullerenes. Combining small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS), dynamic light scattering (DLS), NMR, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, we reveal a pronounced structural compaction upon encapsulation. Both the radius of gyration and the hydrodynamic radius of the dendrimer-fullerene complexes are significantly reduced compared to the free dendrimer. DLS measurements corroborate these results, indicating that the complexes remain monodisperse and free of aggregates. To assess the biocompatibility of these nanocarriers, we evaluated their cytotoxicity in vitro across cancer (HeLa G63, HT-1080) and normal (dermal fibroblasts) human cell lines. The complexes exhibit low cytotoxicity at physiologically relevant concentrations. Cytotoxicity remains low but becomes measurable in a concentration-, time-, and cell-line-dependent manner at supraphysiological doses (≥100 μg/mL). Notably, both compounds demonstrated enhanced cytotoxicity toward the HT-1080 cancer cell line at high concentrations, while showing moderate toxicity in normal cells. These findings highlight the Lys-2Gly dendrimer as a robust, biocompatible nanoplatform, indicating its potential for the encapsulation and delivery of hydrophobic therapeutics and contrast agents.

item.title: Valorization of Rice Husk: Simultaneous Extraction of High-Purity Lignin and Silica via Organic Acid Treatment
item.description:
Abstract
Valorization of elements in agricultural rice husk waste benefits a circular society and can significantly reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) and PM 2.5 emissions from burning and landfilling. The research evinces the extraction of high-purity lignin and silica from rice husk waste using a primary acetic acid solution with a hydrochloric acid catalyst followed by calcination. The new concept reveals that treating rice husks with this acid solution under hydrothermal conditions can combine three essential processes of rice husk pretreatment, lignin extraction, and silica refinement into a single step. Consequently, it can reduce the total processing time. The treatment exhibits a synergistic mechanism wherein acetic acid facilitates dissolution while both HCl and acetic acid cooperatively catalyze the cleavage of lignin bonds. The resulting high-purity lignin nanoparticles (LNPs) obtained under condition A50-H0.3-T120 are hydrophobic, rich in aromatic compounds containing guaiacyl, syringyl, and p-hydroxyphenyl monomers in a ratio of 65.7:0.3:34, and possess a molecular weight of 2129 Da. Meanwhile, the high-purity silica obtained under condition A50-H0.6-T120 forms mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) with a specific surface area of 257 m2/g and a pore volume of 0.36 cm3/g. Finally, a techno-economic evaluation at a small- and medium-enterprise (SME) scale confirms that this process is economically favorable. The gate-to-grave life cycle assessment demonstrates that this process is a sustainable alternative for lignin and silica extraction as its enhanced biodegradable material recovery offsets total greenhouse gas emissions from the process.

item.title: Fabrication of Ag Dot Arrays Using Reusable Porous Alumina Masks
item.description:
Abstract
Ag dot arrays with uniform sizes are functional materials with a wide range of applications, such as substrates for surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) and catalyst nuclei for the formation of semiconductor wires by vapor–liquid–solid (VLS) growth. In this study, we fabricated a reusable porous alumina mask (PAM) to establish a method for the efficient preparation of ordered arrays of Ag dots with uniform sizes. To form an array of Ag dots on a substrate using PAM, the PAM must be thin. However, because thin PAMs are fragile, they lack the mechanical durability required for handling as freestanding films. To address this issue, we fabricated a PAM supported by an Al framework. By placing the resulting PAM in contact with a substrate and depositing Ag, Ag dots of uniform size were formed at positions corresponding to the through holes in the PAM. Although Ag was also deposited on the PAM surface during thermal deposition, it could be selectively dissolved by etching with an aqueous nitric acid solution. Consequently, we were able to repeatedly form arrays of Ag dots of uniform size on a substrate using the same PAM. The Ag dot arrays obtained using this method were also demonstrated to be useful as substrates for the highly sensitive SERS detection of a model molecule.

item.title: Metabolism-Based Bacterial Detection in Water Using First-Principles Modeling and Predictive Machine Learning
item.description:
Abstract
Bacterial contamination in water remains a global health concern.
