This study introduces a simplified and scalable approach for detecting Escherichia coli by coupling bacterial metabolism with predictive modeling. We developed a first-principle model to examine how E. coli consumes glucose as growth and metabolic rates vary over time. Detection time was primarily governed by bacterial growth rates, which exerted a substantially greater influence than variations in glucose consumption. Experimental validation on laboratory and environmental samples was performed using repurposed commercial glucose meters and portable pH sensors to monitor glucose depletion and proton production as indicators of bacterial viability. The model accurately captured these changes and fitted experimental data across varying growth rates induced by temperature differences (R2 ≥ 0.96, RMSE < 0.16 mM). Under optimal conditions, detection occurred within 3 h compared to 23 h under unfavorable conditions. Mixed cultures of Escherichia coli and Bacillus subtilis showed only a marginal effect on detection time relative to temperature. Selective detection of Escherichia coli was achieved using nutrient-specific media. Integrating metabolic data with pH, temperature, and time into machine-learning models enhanced predictive capability, with the decision tree model achieving a mean squared error of 0.0802 and identifying pH, time, and temperature as dominant predictors. Overall, this work redefines bacterial culture as a data-driven, field-ready diagnostic system, transforming simple consumer devices into quantitative biosensors for rapid, low-cost microbial monitoring in environmental and public-health applications.

item.title: A Hydrogen-Bonding Phosphonium/HFIP Catalyst for Efficient CO 2 Conversion into Cyclic Carbonates
item.description:
Abstract
Converting carbon dioxide (CO2) into carbonates is a promising strategy for mitigating carbon emissions. In this study, a series of phosphonium salts/hexafluoroisopropanol (HFIP) catalysts were synthesized and employed in the cycloaddition of CO2 to epoxides to produce cyclic carbonates under mild reaction conditions. The experimental results demonstrated that, at 25 °C and 1 atm CO2 pressure, the catalyst methyltriphenylphosphonium bromide/hexafluoroisopropanol 1/2 (Ph3MePBr/HFIP 1/2) achieved very high yields for monosubstituted (86–96%) as well as 1,1- and 1,2-disubstituted epoxides (66–88%). Density functional theory (DFT) calculations and NMR experiments were employed to elucidate the structure of the Ph3MePBr/HFIP 1/2 catalyst as well as the underlying reaction mechanism. The DFT mechanistic analysis indicated a hydrogen-bond-assisted SN2 pathway, in which the HFIP···Br– pair activates the epoxide and enables efficient CO2 fixation under mild conditions.

item.title: Annoglabrins D–F, Three New ent -Kaurane Diterpenoids from the Annona glabra Fruit Pulp
item.description:
Abstract
Annona glabra L. is a tropical fruit tree distributed across the Americas and Asia, renowned for its diverse traditional therapeutic uses and rich phytochemical profile. Despite its medicinal potential, research on its fruit remains limited, with ambiguities surrounding the distinct constituents of the seeds versus the pulp. To address this gap, the present study focused on the fruit pulp of A. glabra, resulting in the isolation of two new nor-ent-kaurane diterpenoids, annoglabrin D (1) and annoglabrin F (3), and one new ent-kaurane diterpenoid, annoglabrin E (2), along with five known compounds (4–8) of the same skeletal type. Their structures were elucidated via spectroscopic analyses (1D, 2D NMR, HR-ESI-MS) and comparison with previous literature. DP4 probability and ECD spectrum were deployed to identify the absolute configuration of compounds 1–3. The in vitro nitric oxide production inhibitory assay indicated 3 (IC50 48.1 μM) and 8 (IC50 51.8 μM) as moderate inhibitors in comparison with L-NMMA (IC50 12.9 μM), while the others were inactive. Compound 8 demonstrated potent cytotoxicity against KB (IC50 19.7 μM) and HepG2 (IC50 16.4 μM) cancer cell lines, in comparison with ellipticine (IC50 1.91, 1.95 μM, respectively). These findings were corroborated by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations, revealing the efficient and stable binding interactions of 3 and 8 with proteins associated with key inflammatory mediators (iNOS, IL-6, TNF-α, COX-2, IL-1β), transcription factors (NF-κB, Nrf2), and the KB and HepG2 cancer cell lines. The simulations predicted the contribution of specific functional groups in compounds 3 and 8, particularly the C-4 methyl, C-16 ketone, and acetoxymethyl carbonyl in 3, as well as the methyl ester moiety at C-16 and the carboxyl group (−COOH) at C-4 in 8, in mediating these compounds’ stable and effective interactions.

item.title: Integrated Toxicological, Network Toxicology, and Molecular Simulation Assessment of Inhalation Toxicity and Mechanisms of HFO-1336mzz(E) as an SF 6 Alternative Insulating Gas
item.description:
Abstract
HFO-1336mzz(E) is a novel environmentally friendly insulating gas with a low global warming potential and favorable dielectric properties, and it has been regarded as an important potential substitute for sulfur hexafluoride (SF6). However, its systemic toxicological characteristics and underlying mechanisms under inhalation exposure remain insufficiently investigated. To address this issue, the present study, for the first time, systematically evaluated the biological safety of HFO-1336mzz(E) by integrating multilevel toxicological assessment with molecular mechanistic analysis. Acute inhalation toxicity, bone marrow micronucleus, and embryonic developmental toxicity experiments were conducted, and the potential toxic effects and mechanisms were comprehensively analyzed through the integration of molecular docking, functional enrichment analysis, and molecular dynamics simulations. The results showed that the 4-h LC50 of HFO-1336mzz(E) in both male and female rats was approximately 31,600 ppm, which is classified as Category 5 according to the Globally Harmonized System (GHS). Under high-dose exposure, the primary target organs were the lung and liver, characterized mainly by acute tissue responses dominated by congestion. Following low-to-moderate dose exposure, the physiological condition of the animals gradually recovered, and no extensive structural damage to tissues was observed. Under short-term inhalation exposure and repeated exposure during pregnancy, this compound did not induce significant genotoxicity, while only limited developmental toxicity effects were observed under the tested conditions. Further mechanistic analyses suggested that its potential toxic effects may involve disturbances in heme-dependent redox systems and energy metabolism pathways. These effects may be associated with the regulation of oxidative stress and inflammatory signaling pathways, which could subsequently influence local microcirculatory homeostasis and tissue perfusion status. This study systematically provides insights into the biological basis of the acute inhalation toxicity of HFO-1336mzz(E). Moreover, a multidimensional toxicological evaluation and mechanistic analysis framework for novel environmentally friendly insulating gases was established, providing important scientific support for risk assessment, safety standard formulation, and refined management in engineering applications.

item.title: Sodium Alginate–Based Coatings Safeguard Garlic Cloves and Provide Controlled Biostimulant Delivery to Improve Agronomic Performance
item.description:
Abstract
The application of biopolymers derived from natural sources as agricultural coating materials represents a promising strategy for improving propagation efficiency and seedling establishment. This approach can enhance moisture retention and mechanical protection while enabling the controlled release of bioactive compounds, such as biostimulants. The present study evaluated a sodium alginate–based polymeric matrix and its corresponding films, with and without the incorporation of tryptophol, for coating garlic cloves belonging to two distinct vigor classes. Physicochemical analyses revealed a predominance of mannuronic acid over guluronic acid in the polymeric matrix, suggesting that its structural characteristics may contribute to the protective properties of the coating. Furthermore, the incorporation of tryptophol, a biostimulatory compound, significantly influenced the physicochemical properties of the alginate films, particularly their water absorption and swelling behavior. Bioassays conducted with garlic propagules demonstrated that small cloves treated with the biopolymer–biostimulant combination exhibited reduced activation of oxidative defense mechanisms, whereas large cloves subjected to the same treatment showed improved yield and quality. Both vigor classes exhibited a lower incidence of physiological disorders following treatment with either the biopolymer–biostimulant combination or the biostimulant alone. Overall, this biotechnology-based approach is innovative, cost-effective, and readily adaptable to agricultural applications, offering a sustainable strategy for improving crop establishment and productivity.

item.title: Cancer-Associated Fibroblast-Derived Exosomal circTBPL1 Regulates NSCLC Cell Stemness and Cisplatin Resistance via the miR-152-3p/Gli1 Axis
item.description:
Abstract
Drug resistance and cancer stem cell maintenance drive poor outcomes in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet the role of cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF)-derived exosomal circular RNAs remains insufficiently defined. This study investigated whether CAF-derived exosomal circTBPL1 regulates NSCLC stemness and cisplatin resistance through the miR-152-3p/Gli1 axis. Exosomal circRNAs from CAFs and normal fibroblasts were profiled by high-throughput sequencing, and circTBPL1 was validated using qRT-PCR, RNase R, actinomycin D, and fluorescence in situ hybridization. Functional assays, xenograft models, dual-luciferase reporter assays, RNA immunoprecipitation, RNA pull-down, rescue experiments, and TCGA analyses were performed. circTBPL1 was enriched in CAF-derived exosomes and displayed circular RNA stability and cytoplasmic localization. CAF-derived exosomal circTBPL1 promoted NSCLC cell proliferation, migration, invasion, tumor-sphere formation, stemness marker expression, and cisplatin resistance. circTBPL1 silencing in CAFs reduced cisplatin IC50 values, inhibited resistant-cell proliferation, and suppressed xenograft growth. Mechanistically, circTBPL1 acted as a competing endogenous RNA by binding miR-152-3p, relieving repression of Gli1 and activating Hedgehog-related resistance signaling. miR-152-3p inhibition or Gli1 overexpression partially reversed circTBPL1-knockdown effects. TCGA analysis linked high Gli1 expression with poorer survival in lung adenocarcinoma, supporting circTBPL1 as a potential biomarker candidate and therapeutic target requiring further clinical validation.

item.title: Hydrophobic Guests Influencing Assembling of Six Water Molecules
item.description:
Abstract
Assemblies of six water molecules serve as a pivotal hydrogen-bonded unit for understanding the bulk properties of water and have been extensively studied. The energetics of various forms of different geometries have been investigated earlier. However, the influence of stimuli and hydrophobic molecules on the assemblies of six water molecules has not been understood yet. In this study, the role of different hydrophobic molecules in stabilizing different geometries of assemblies of six water molecules was determined from geometrical optimization using DFT calculations with the method ωB97X using def2-TZV basis set. Different geometries such as open-book, closed-bag, prism, and double-envelope were stabilized by one or more hydrophobic molecules in assemblies with six water molecules. There are infinite possibilities among the open-book geometries, where incremental differences in bond parameters or hydrophobic effects cause disturbances to the geometries of hydrogen bonds. The changes in the scheme of interactions in the assembly of six water molecules guided by O–H···O hydrogen bonds largely influenced the geometries. Weak interactions such as C–H···O, O–H···π, and O–H···F–C interactions contributed to such subtle changes and influenced the geometries. Energies of optimized geometries have suggested a net gain in each assembly, and the Gibbs free energies of formation were less than 1 kJ/mol. Aliphatic and aromatic hydrocarbons, fluoro-hydrocarbons, phenols, pyridine analogues, etc., influenced the geometry of their assemblies with six molecules of water.

item.title: Cd 2+ Substitution Modulates the Rate of Flavin Reduction in D-2-Hydroxyglutarate Dehydrogenase from Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1
item.description:
Abstract
Pseudomonas aeruginosa D-2-hydroxyglutarate dehydrogenase (PaD2HGDH; EC 1.1.99.39) is a Zn2+- and FAD-dependent metallo-flavoenzyme that oxidizes α-hydroxy acid substrates through a metal-triggered flavin reduction mechanism. In this work, Zn2+ was replaced by Cd2+ to define how metal identity governs substrate capture, flavin reduction, and conformational gating during catalysis of PaD2HGDH. Relative to the native Zn2+ enzyme, Cd2+ lowered catalytic efficiency for substrate capture (kcat/Km) by ∼10-fold (∼10,000 to 1,000 M–1 s–1) and decreased the rate of flavin-reduction (kred) by ∼5-fold (68 s–1 to 13 s–1), with the Kd value increasing by ∼2-fold. These results are consistent with the larger size of Cd2+, which alters the optimal orientation of the substrate C2 atom relative to the FAD N5 atom. The solvent-viscosity effect indicated that, in the Cd2+ enzyme, kcat, kcat/Km, and kred follow normal hyperbolic viscosity dependences, whereas Kd varies linearly with a slope > 1. This pattern suggests a solvent-sensitive internal isomerization that becomes rate-relevant and conformationally gates both substrate binding and flavin reduction with D-malate as a model substrate. In contrast, the Zn2+ enzyme shows linear viscosity effects consistent with an internal isomerization step that is hidden by slower product release. Together with prior results from Ni2+ substitution, these findings support a unified model in which the divalent metal center not only activates the α-hydroxy acid but also tunes metal–ligand geometry and electrostatics to reshape the ES ⇌ ES* landscape, thereby modulating binding and intramolecular electron transfer to FAD. This mechanistic framework informs metal-dependent flavin reduction and supports the development of metal-chelating inhibitors targeting PaD2HGDH to help address multidrug resistance in P. aeruginosa.

item.title: Geochronology, Geochemistry, and Sr–Nd–Pb–Hf Isotopes of Late Triassic Granitoids in the Qiongdongnan Basin, Northern South China Sea: Insights into Petrogenesis and Tectonic Implications
item.description:
Abstract
The South China Sea (SCS) has experienced a complex tectono-magmatic evolution since the Paleozoic, making its Late Paleozoic–Early Mesozoic tectonic evolution poorly constrained and widely debated. We report zircon ages, whole-rock geochemistry, and Sr–Nd–Pb–Hf isotopes of the granitoids intersected in Well Y8-3b in the Songnan Low Uplift, Qiongdongnan Basin, northern SCS margin, to constrain their petrogenesis and tectonic implications. The granitoids comprise granodiorite and monzogranite, with zircon U–Pb ages of 231 Ma and 230 Ma, respectively. The granitoids are high-K calc-alkaline and peraluminous, with Fe numbers of 0.71–0.79 (average = 0.75). They are enriched in light rare earth elements (LREE) and large-ion lithophile elements (LILE), depleted in high field strength elements (HFSE), and exhibit pronounced negative Eu anomalies. Geochemical and isotopic data indicate that the granitoids are ferroan I-type granites derived from a common magma source. The granodiorite likely represents an earlier magmatic product, whereas the monzogranite formed through subsequent magmatic differentiation. The granitoids were derived from hybrid magmas generated by mixing approximately 45% SCS mantle-derived magma with 55% crustal melt, and were emplaced in a post-collisional extensional setting. These new and compiled data reveal that the South China–Indochina amalgamation was a protracted process, evolving from syn-collisional assembly (254–243 Ma) to post-collisional extension (242–225 Ma).

item.title: Basin-Scale Heterogeneity in CO 2 Geological Storage: Mechanisms, Prediction, and Management
item.description:
Abstract
Large-scale CO2 geological storage is evolving from stand-alone sites toward million-tonne-scale, clustered, and basin-coordinated deployment, making basin-scale heterogeneity a key constraint on capacity utilization, sustained injection, and long-term storage security. However, existing studies have largely focused on individual reservoirs, capacity estimation, or localized risks, while a systematic review integrating tectono-sedimentary evolution, reservoir–caprock assemblages, fault-controlled hydrodynamics, and multisite interference remains lacking. Based on representative sedimentary basins and engineering projects, this study reviews multisource characterization, scale transformation, multiphysics coupling, probabilistic prediction, monitoring-informed updating, and coordinated management within a “geological foundation–storage performance–prediction and regulation” framework. The results indicate that reservoir–caprock discontinuities, fault connectivity, and pressure boundaries jointly control dynamic storage capacity, pressure footprints, plume migration, trapping efficiency, and leakage risk; although multilayer utilization can increase storage capacity, it may intensify pressure superposition and cross-formational flow. This study proposes development pathways centered on pressure-constrained capacity assessment, probabilistic prediction, full-life-cycle simulation, and basin digital twins, providing a basis for regional resource allocation, coordinated multiproject injection, and long-term risk management.

item.title: Long-Term Biodistribution and Safety Profile of Laser-Generated Gold Nanoparticles Following High-Dose Administration in Mice
item.description:
Abstract
Gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) have emerged as versatile agents for a wide range of biomedical applications, including imaging, diagnostics, and therapy. While their use in modalities such as CT imaging and radiotherapy is particularly promising, these applications require high systemic doses (≥500 mg Au/kg), necessitating thorough evaluation of long-term biodistribution and safety profiles. Here, we present a comprehensive one-year assessment of Polyethylene glycol (PEG) -coated laser-synthesized AuNPs (mean core diameter ∼8 nm). After intravenous administration at a high dose, biodistribution was evaluated in healthy mice (n = 8; 874 ± 56 mg Au/kg) using a serial CT imaging, with terminal ICP-AES validation, blood biochemistry, and histology performed in 5 of these animals. AuNPs exhibited prolonged blood circulation (half-life 21 ± 3 h) and accumulated predominantly in reticuloendothelial organs: 42.2 ± 3.6%ID/cm3 in the liver and 40.2 ± 3.3%ID/cm3 in the spleen, with one-year retention of 77.5% and 83.1%, respectively. Despite substantial hepatic and splenic retention, no histopathological changes were detected in any major organs, including kidney and liver. Serum biochemical markers of liver, kidney, and pancreatic function revealed no statistically significant differences between the treated and control groups. Only a slight elevation in aspartate aminotransferase (AST) was observed in two treated animals (184.1 and 187.8 U/L vs 118.3 ± 18.4 U/L in the control group), while all other liver function markers (ALT, alkaline phosphatase, bilirubin) remained unaltered. Additionally, tumor uptake was evaluated in two separate cohorts of mice bearing subcutaneous tumor models, mammary adenocarcinoma Ca755 (n = 3, 809 ± 28 mg Au/kg) and melanoma B16F10 (n = 3, 814 ± 45 mg Au/kg). AuNPs accumulated in tumor tissue, reaching 9.4 ± 1.9%ID/cm3 for Ca755 and 5.3 ± 1.1%ID/cm3 for B16F10. Overall, these results provide insight into the safety profile and tumor uptake of laser-synthesized AuNPs, supporting their potential as a platform for novel radiosensitizers and contrast agents.

item.title: Epoxy and Vinyl Silane Functionalization of Graphene Nanoplatelets
item.description:
Abstract
Functionalization of low-oxygen-content graphene nanoplatelets (GNP; C/O > 9:1) remains challenging due to the need to preserve the intrinsic transport properties associated with their high sp2 carbon content. Silanization provides an effective route to introduce reactive surface functionalities via hydrolysis–condensation reactions with surface hydroxyl groups. Here, the successful functionalization of GNP using vinyltrimethoxysilane (VTMS) and 3-glycidoxypropyltrimethoxysilane (G-PTMS) was achieved via a condensation silanization reaction or a pathway dependent on the R-group of each silane. Comprehensive characterization including X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), Raman spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction (XRD), electron microscopy, and thermogravimetric analysis coupled with mass spectrometry (TGA-MS) confirmed successful grafting of the silane species. This approach demonstrates that silanization is a viable and versatile strategy for functionalizing GNPs with reactive vinyl and epoxy functionalities which are then available for cross-linking with polymers and other substrates.

item.title: Biogenic Hydroxyapatite/ZnO Heterostructures: Photocatalytic Degradation of Dye Mixtures and Antibacterial Activity
item.description:
Abstract
In this work, biogenic HAp/ZnO heterostructures were synthesized by a microwave-assisted hydrothermal method using marine shell waste as the calcium precursor for hydroxyapatite production. ZnO was incorporated at 20, 30, 40, and 50 wt %. XRD and FTIR confirmed the coexistence of HAp and ZnO phases, while UV–Vis/DRS indicated optical absorption suitable for photocatalytic activation. FE-SEM and TEM/HRTEM analyses revealed morphological changes and confirmed the nanostructured character of the heterostructures. BET showed a significant increase in the specific surface area of H40ZN, and PL and EIS analyses indicated improved charge separation and reduced electron–hole recombination. Photocatalytic activity was evaluated by degrading crystal violet, malachite green, and their mixture under UV–C irradiation, with the best sample also tested under solar light. H40ZN exhibited the highest performance, reaching 71% degradation for CV, 74% for MG, and 83% for MIX under solar irradiation. Reusability tests showed only a slight efficiency decrease after four cycles, with no structural changes detected by XRD. Scavenger tests and EPR analyses indicated that •O2–, h+, and •OH were the main reactive species. The heterostructures also showed antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus. These results demonstrate the potential of biogenic HAp/ZnO heterostructures for environmental remediation and bacterial control.

item.title: Electronic Modulation of Bromide and Iodide Recognition in Functionalized Hexacationic Cages: A Comparative Theoretical Study of meta - and para -Frameworks
item.description:
Abstract
Understanding the factors governing anion recognition is essential for the rational design of supramolecular receptors with enhanced affinity and selectivity. The recognition of Br– and I– by two families of hexacationic cages, meta- (MH6+) and para- (PH6+) derivatives bearing electron-donating (−NH2) or electron-withdrawing (−NO2) substituents at different chemical positions, was investigated using Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations. The preferential recognition of Br– over I– is primarily associated with its smaller ionic radius, which enables a better geometric fit within the cavity and consequently leads to reduced Pauli repulsion together with stronger electrostatic and orbital interactions. Most substitutions weaken host–guest recognition primarily because of less favorable electrostatic and orbital interactions, such as (C or, chiefly, N)–H···Br– and (heteroatom or C)···Br–; however, specific substituents significantly enhance Br– binding. The para-derivatives exhibit the strongest interaction energies owing to the cooperative reinforcement of non-covalent (C or, mainly, N)–H···Br– interactions. In contrast, one meta-derivative follows a distinct recognition mechanism, in which the conventional Br– → σ*(N–H) interaction is replaced by charge transfer toward a σ*(C–NO2) orbital, giving rise to an unusually strong C···Br– interaction with partial covalent character and pronounced orbital stabilization. These findings reveal how the cage framework and electronic substitution cooperatively modulate chemical interactions, providing molecular design principles for highly efficient supramolecular halide receptors.

item.title: Structural Characterization of Mycobacterium tuberculosis IspQ Reveals Membrane-Dependent Stabilization of Its Conserved Electron-Transfer Cofactor Network
item.description:
Abstract
Mycobacterium tuberculosis persistence in granulomas depends on lipid catabolism through the β-oxidation-coupled respiratory pathway, which requires the essential membrane-associated protein IspQ, encoded by Rv0338c. Although IspQ is a genetically and chemically validated drug target, its structural organization and membrane-dependent function remain unknown. Using AlphaFold3 structure prediction, cofactor mapping, evolutionary conservation analysis, and atomistic molecular dynamics simulations, we show that IspQ adopts an EtfD-like fold containing four iron–sulfur clusters, a heme b, and a menaquinone-binding pocket, mapped from the experimental EtfD structure, to form a continuous electron-transfer relay, with all 25 coordinating residues corresponding one-to-one with their experimentally assigned counterparts. Simulations across three independent replicates in each of three membrane systems reveal that the native mycobacterial membrane produces the lowest global conformational deviation, reduces the flexibility of cofactor-coordinating residues by 24% relative to a simple bilayer, and maintains the catalytic menaquinone-binding heme pocket in a geometry closest to that of the cofactor-loaded experimental structure. Native lipids form persistent interactions with IspQ, defining conserved protein–lipid interfaces. These findings establish a structural and dynamic framework for IspQ, reveal membrane-dependent modulation of its electron-transfer machinery, and identify these interfaces as candidate sites for structure-guided antitubercular drug discovery.

item.title: Solving the Computational Peptide Design Puzzle: Challenges and Opportunities
item.description:
Abstract
Peptides are increasingly recognized as promising therapeutics, antimicrobial agents, and supramolecular biomaterials due to the remarkable versatility encoded in their amino acid sequences. However, the rational design of peptides remains challenging because sequence-structure–function relationships are not yet fully understood. Experimental exploration of peptide chemical space is inherently limited by the vast number of possible sequences and the complexity of resolving peptide behavior at molecular resolution. Computational methods, particularly molecular dynamics simulations and, more recently, machine learning and deep learning, have emerged as promising strategies to address these limitations. Although computational objectives differ, ranging from binding poses and biological activity to self-assembly propensity and supramolecular morphologies, they share common challenges associated with methodological heterogeneity, incomplete experimental metadata, insufficient benchmarking, and the lack of standardized and interoperable data sets. Here, we present our perspective on the main challenges in the computational study and design of peptides and discuss how collective efforts toward standardized data generation and data-driven discovery frameworks may help advance the field.

item.title: Role of Binder Ductility in Enhancing the Green Body Integrity of Ceramic Vat Photopolymerization
item.description:
Abstract
This study investigates the influence of photocurable acrylate binder mechanical properties on the fabrication of high-density zirconia ceramic parts via vat photopolymerization (VPP) to resolve persistent defects in green bodies by shifting focus from traditional slurry rheology to binder mechanics. By evaluating the transition from rigid to ductile acrylate binders in high-solid-loading zirconia VPP, the research focuses on the mechanical response of green bodies and validates performance through the assessment of relative density, hardness, and fracture toughness of sintered components. A critical trade-off was identified where binders with high neat mechanical strength led to early particle percolation and microcracking, whereas flexible binders created a pliable network that effectively dissipated internal stresses. Although flexible binders slightly reduced theoretical packing density by 5–10%, they enabled the production of defect-free zirconia parts sintered to 98% relative density, achieving a hardness of 13.4 GPa and fracture toughness of 4.8 MPa·m1/2. Ultimately, the study establishes binder flexibility rather than neat mechanical strength as the decisive design parameter for highly loaded suspensions, providing a validated framework for developing versatile binders suitable for both ceramic and metallic VPP systems.

item.title: Axially Chiral ( R )-BINOL-, ( R )-BINAM-, and ( R )-NOBIN-Stabilized Palladium Nanoparticles for Highly Enantioselective Asymmetric Suzuki-Miyaura Cross-Coupling Reactions
item.description:
Abstract
Chiral palladium nanoparticles (PdNPs) stabilized by axially chiral 1,1′-bi-2-naphthol ((R)-BINOL), (R)-[1,1′-binaphthalene]-2,2′-diamine ((R)-BINAM), and (R)-2-amino-1,1′-binaphthalen-2-ol ((R)-NOBIN) ligands were synthesized and evaluated as heterogeneous catalysts for asymmetric Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling reactions. Structural and spectroscopic analyses confirmed the formation of crystalline PdNPs with narrow size distributions (2.4–2.7 nm) and ligand-induced surface chirality. Under the optimized conditions, the catalysts consistently provided high enantioselectivities, reaching ≥99% ee over a broad substrate scope comprising diverse aryl halides and boronic acids. Enantioinduction originates from the chiral environment at the nanoparticle surface, whereas catalytic efficiency is primarily determined by the steric and electronic properties of the substrate and the identity of the leaving group. (R)-BINAM-stabilized PdNPs provided superior conversions, which can be attributed to the two amine (−NH2) groups in (R)-BINAM that enable stronger metal–ligand interactions at the Pd surface. Poisoning, hot filtration, and recycling experiments support predominantly heterogeneous catalysis and demonstrate retention of activity and enantioselectivity over multiple cycles. These findings establish chiral PdNPs as efficient, reusable, and highly enantioselective catalysts for the synthesis of axially chiral biaryls.

item.title: Cluster Incorporation and Critical Nucleus Size in Crystal Growth: Particle-Resolved Observations Using Colloidal Crystals
item.description:
Abstract
We investigate cluster incorporation and dissolution events in two-dimensional colloidal crystals using particle-resolved imaging and machine learning. Particle positions were identified from microscopy images using an object-detection method. The obtained particle positions were used to track individual particles and identify changes in cluster size. We analyzed the statistics of cluster incorporation and dissolution events as a function of the size change associated with each event. The observed event frequency is well described by the cluster size distribution. These results demonstrate that particle-resolved, machine-learning analysis can provide a quantitative approach to investigating cluster dynamics in colloidal crystallization. Furthermore, the analysis provides an estimate of the kinetic critical nucleus size. Under quasi-equilibrium conditions, we show that the kinetic critical size coincides with the thermodynamic critical size, even in the presence of a cluster-mediated growth pathway. Our experimental estimate of the kinetic critical nucleus size is consistent in order of magnitude with the thermodynamic estimate.

item.title: Substrate-Dependent Cryogenic and UV Performance of AlGaN/AlN/GaN HEMTs and Photodetectors
item.description:
Abstract
AlGaN/AlN/GaN high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) and metal–semiconductor–metal photodetectors (MSM-PDs) were integrated on Al2O3 and 4H-SiC substrates to quantify the impact of substrate selection on cryogenic electrical stability and ultraviolet (UV) optoelectronic performance. The HEMT/SiC structure exhibited a higher peak transconductance (gm) of 1.56 mS/2.34 mS at 300 K/130 K compared to the HEMT/Al2O3 structure (1.27 mS/1.83 mS). At 300 K, the gate-source voltage corresponding to peak gm was −0.3 V for the HEMT/SiC compared to −2.1 V for the HEMT/Al2O3, indicating different strain-induced polarization effects. For integrated sensing, the peak relative spectral response wavelengths were observed at 300 nm (on Al2O3) and 370 nm (on SiC). High-resolution characterization confirms that improved crystal quality and carrier transport in SiC-based heterostructures result from reduced lattice mismatch at the GaN/SiC interface. These findings establish the AlGaN/AlN/GaN-on-SiC platform as a compelling architecture for high-efficiency, switching GaN electronics and integrated cryogenic optoelectronic applications.

item.title: Development of a Vibrio natriegens -Based Plate-Clearing Assay for Rapid Screening of PET-Hydrolyzing Enzymes
item.description:
Abstract
Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) is a major contributor to plastic waste. Enzymatic PET degradation offers a sustainable recycling approach, but screening for effective enzymes remains challenging. Herein, we established an experimental plate-clearing assay using Vibrio natriegens, exploiting its protein secretion system to rapidly identify catalytic activity without time-consuming downstream processing. To validate the assay’s robustness, we tested variants of Fusarium solanipisi cutinase (FsC) and found that one variant, T45P, exhibited 3-fold higher PET-film degradation yield than the wild type and favored the production of terephthalic acid. As a further test case, we screened an error-prone polymerase chain reaction (PCR) library of FsC using the assay, obtaining a 25% hit rate after screening 150 colonies. This demonstrates the scalability of the method to large enzyme libraries.

item.title: Integrated Phenotyping Reveals Trait-Specific Bacillus Modulation of Soybean Water-Deficit Responses
item.description:
Abstract
Water deficit restricts soybean (Glycine max (L.) Merr.) performance by reducing leaf expansion, water status, carbon assimilation, photosystem II activity, and leaf optical properties. Here, soybean plants were grown under four fixed irrigation volumes corresponding to 100, 50, 25, and 0% of the substrate field-capacity reference volume (W100, W50, W25, and W0), with or without rhizosphere-applied Bacillus subtilis + Bacillus amyloliquefaciens before water restriction. Plant growth, relative water content (RWC), thermal and VIS–NIR–SWIR optical traits, photosynthetic pigments, A–PPFD and A–Ci gas exchange, chlorophyll a fluorescence, OJIP transients, microscopy, and principal component analysis were integrated. Two-way ANOVA showed that water availability was the dominant source of variation, whereas Bacillus and water × Bacillus effects were trait dependent. Bacillus produced a severity-dependent phenotype, with the clearest whole-plant benefit under W50: leaf area increased from 526.3 ± 32.9 to 620.9 ± 45.3 cm2 plant–1 and total biomass from 5.63 ± 0.23 to 6.89 ± 0.28 g plant–1; total chlorophyll also increased by 63.2–93.5% across Bacillus-treated water regimes. However, A–PPFD-derived Amax declined from 13.66 ± 1.57 μmol CO2 m–2 s–1 under W100 to near-zero values under W0 and W0B. In contrast, A–Ci traits were more responsive: Vcmax increased by 106.9% in W100B and showed a 74.7% numerical, nonsignificant increase in W50B (p = 0.058), while W0B showed higher Fv/Fm relative to W0 under severe dehydration. PCA separated treatments across the first two components (51.79%) mainly along a drought-severity axis and secondarily by Bacillus-associated photochemical and structural shifts. These findings indicate that rhizosphere-applied Bacillus acts as a trait-specific modulator of soybean drought physiology, with growth benefits most evident under intermediate water restriction.

item.title: Fermi-Level Modulation in Graphene Sensors Revealed by Voltage-Dependent Raman Spectroscopy and 3D Waterfall Response Mapping
item.description:
Abstract
The electronic properties of graphene sensors are governed by the position of the Fermi level, which determines the carrier concentration and consequently controls the electrical conductivity and sensing performance. Although Fermi-level modulation is widely recognized as the fundamental mechanism of graphene-based sensing, its direct experimental correlation with the dynamic sensing response has remained insufficiently explored. In this work, we demonstrate that Raman spectroscopy provides a direct, nondestructive method for quantifying the relative Fermi-level modulation through systematic shifts of the G and 2D Raman bands associated with changes in carrier concentration. The Raman analysis reveals reversible electrical tuning of the graphene electronic structure under source-drain voltage without introducing structural defects, allowing quantitative estimation of the Fermi-level relative displacement. To investigate the dynamic behavior of the same electronic states during sensor operation, low-frequency time–frequency waterfall spectroscopy was employed under chemical and optical stimulation. The results demonstrate that external stimuli induce transient perturbations of the graphene Fermi level, producing characteristic conductivity fluctuations that depend on the magnitude and kinetics of carrier-density modulation. The combination of static (Raman spectroscopy) and dynamic (waterfall fluctuation) analyses establishes a unified sensing mechanism linking Fermi-level modulation → carrier concentration → conductivity fluctuations → sensor response. These findings demonstrate that evaluation of the Fermi level is essential not only for understanding the intrinsic electronic structure of graphene but also for interpreting and optimizing its real-time chemical and optical sensing performance, providing a comprehensive framework for the design of next-generation graphene sensors.

item.title: Insights into Desalination Performance of Spacing-Tunable Laminated MXene Membranes via Molecular Dynamics and Machine Learning
item.description:
Abstract
Developing desalination membranes that combine high water permeance with high ion rejection remains important for freshwater production. Laminated MXene membranes are promising because their surface chemistry and channel dimensions are tunable, yet the respective roles of sheet-edge openings and interlayer spacing in staggered channels remain unclear. We performed molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of 242 O- and F-terminated Ti3C2 MXene membrane systems, varying the sheet-edge gap and interlayer spacing, d, from 6 to 16 Å. Machine learning (ML) analysis identified gap as the main structural variable governing water permeance and the extent of ion penetration, while d further regulated transport within the interlayer channels. Water and ion density distributions showed that gap primarily controlled entry into the laminated membrane, whereas d affected postentry transport and ion hydration. Na–Ow radial distribution functions and hydration-loss analyses indicated that narrow interlayer channels mainly perturbed the second hydration shell of Na+. Under matched geometries, surface termination produced weaker and more localized changes in water and ion distributions. These results distinguish entry control by the sheet-edge gap from postentry regulation by interlayer spacing and provide molecular guidance for designing spacing-tunable laminated MXene membranes.

item.title: Biomimetic Fabrication and Osteogenic Efficacy Evaluation of Tilapia-Derived Collagen-Based Artificial Bone Scaffolds
item.description:
Abstract
Inspired by the natural biomineralization processes observed in terrestrial vertebrates, this study independently designed an in vitro mineralization system to activate nucleation sites within tilapia fish collagen, facilitating the fabrication of biomimetic bone substitutes. Through lyophilization and molding techniques, a three-dimensional porous scaffold with a defined spatial architecture and adequate mechanical integrity was successfully constructed. Subsequently, the physicochemical properties, biocompatibility, and biodegradation characteristics of the prepared fish collagen-based artificial bone (FC-AB) were evaluated and compared to relevant standards. Furthermore, a rat tibial critical-sized defect model was employed to assess the in vivo bone regeneration capacity. The results demonstrated that the FC-AB scaffold possesses an ideal porous microstructure, excellent biocompatibility, and controllable degradation characteristics. Notably, it significantly promoted the osteogenesis and functional restoration of the bone defect. In conclusion, this research confirms the feasibility of utilizing fish collagen as a precursor for in vitro mineralization, yielding artificial bone materials with superior structural mimicry, mechanical competence, and osteoinductive potential, thereby positioning it as a promising candidate for bone tissue engineering.

item.title: Synergistic Absorption Mechanism in Flexible Polymer Composites Reinforced with Rare Earth Cobaltite and Molybdenum Carbide for EMI Shielding Applications
item.description:
Abstract
The sudden growth of digital devices and fifth-generation (5G) communication systems has generated increasing concerns regarding electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding in advanced technological applications, due to the high necessity for development of flexible, lightweight and efficient shielding materials. In this study, low thickness polymer composite films based on poly(vinylidene fluoride) polymer that is incorporated with gadolinium cobaltite and molybdenum carbide fillers were successfully fabricated through a solution casting technique. The chemical, structural, and morphological characteristics of the composite films were investigated using XRD, FTIR, FESEM, HR-TEM, tensile strength and contact angle. Thermal stability was assessed through thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), and electromagnetic properties were evaluated in terms of complex permittivity and permeability across the X-band frequency range. The EMI shielding was examined in terms of shielding effectiveness due to absorption, reflection, and transmission and further validated using CST software. The selected composite film with an ultralow thickness of ∼0.15 mm exhibited a maximum EMI shielding efficiency of ∼49 dB in the X-band region with the absorption dominant shielding as the primary attenuation mechanism. The composite films displayed an enhanced mechanical strength and hydrophobicity behavior, making them suitable for flexible and durable shielding applications. These results suggest that the developed PVDF/GdCoO3/Mo2C composite films are promising candidates for advanced electromagnetic interference shielding applications in wearable electronics, stealth technology, and defense systems.

item.title: Terbium-Doped Graphene Quantum Dots: A Highly Efficient and Selective Fluorescent Nanoprobe for Vanillin Detection
item.description:
Abstract
Vanillin, an extensively used flavoring compound in our daily life, may lead to health problems when overused, adulterated, or poorly controlled in commercial settings, necessitating the development of sensitive and rapid detection techniques. In this work, terbium-doped graphene quantum dots (Tb-GQD) were synthesized using carbonization and chemical conjugation methods for developing an efficient fluorescent probe for vanillin detection. The structural and optical characteristics of Tb-GQD confirm that terbium is doped in GQDs, without disturbing the sp2 graphitic core of GQD, and efficient energy transfer from GQD to Tb3+ was observed from the photoluminescence emission studies. Upon addition of vanillin to Tb-GQD, a decrease in fluorescence emission intensity and a change in lifetime were observed, suggesting a dynamic, photoinduced electron transfer mechanism. The Tb-GQD shows a linear detection range of 0.2–85 μM with a detection limit of 13.2 nM. The synthesized fluorescent probe shows excellent selectivity, and was implemented in real-sample analysis with a good recovery range of 96.4–100.06% and an RSD below 3.6%. These findings show that Tb-GQD will serve as an efficient platform for detecting vanillin.

item.title: Hydrogel Formulation Containing PLGA Nanoparticles for Controlled Codelivery of Vitamin D and Chlorhexidine as a Promising Approach for Postdental Implant Applications
item.description:
Abstract
Tooth loss can have a significant impact on oral health and quality of life, and dental implants are currently the standard option for its replacement. However, implant failure still occurs, with bacterial infection and inadequate osseointegration being the most common causes. In this context, vitamin D3 was selected for its known pro-osteogenic role, while chlorhexidine (CHX), a widely used antiseptic with recognized bactericidal and bacteriostatic activity, was chosen as the antimicrobial component. To enable controlled and localized delivery of both molecules, two types of poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) nanoparticles (NPs) were developed, CHX- and vitamin D3-loaded NPs. The produced NPs displayed an average size of 140 nm, a polydispersity index below 0.2, and negative ζ-potentials. Encapsulation efficiency reached 39% for CHX and 98% for vitamin D3, and transmission electron microscopy confirmed their spherical morphology. In vitro release assays demonstrated an initial burst release followed by a slower release phase for 3 days under simulated physiological conditions, while stability tests under storage conditions showed preservation of the nanoformulations’ physicochemical properties for at least 2 months. Antibacterial assays against Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) and Staphylococcus epidermidis (S. epidermidis) confirmed the antimicrobial effect of CHX-loaded NPs. Cytotoxicity studies in human dermal fibroblasts indicated that combining both formulations (50 nM vitamin D3 and 0.01% w/v CHX) was safe. To facilitate application in the oral cavity, the NP mixture was incorporated into a nontoxic, pseudoplastic hydrogel. These findings highlight the potential of this nanohydrogel as a localized therapeutic approach capable of providing localized antimicrobial activity and supporting conditions favorable to osseointegration, paving the way for improved long-term implant outcomes.

item.title: Pro-Apoptotic and Autophagy-Inducing Activity of Novel 1,4-Naphthoquinone Derivatives against Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma without ROS Generation
item.description:
Abstract
Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) remains a major global health burden, and current platinum-based chemotherapeutics are constrained by systemic toxicity and acquired resistance, motivating the search for novel antitumor agents. Naphthoquinones are a privileged scaffold in anticancer drug discovery. Here, we report the synthesis of 18 1,4-naphthoquinone esters (1–18), 14 of which are novel, and their first evaluation as anticancer agents against three OSCC cell lines (SCC-4, SCC-9, and SCC-25) and primary human gingival fibroblasts. Derivative 14 emerged as the lead compound, displaying a geometric mean IC50 of 5.0 μM and a geometric mean selectivity index of 9.15, outperforming, in terms of selectivity, the chemotherapeutic standards carboplatin, lapachol, and shikonin. Mechanistically, 14 induced cell death through a combined apoptotic–autophagic pathway, evidenced by membrane blebbing, G2/M arrest, sub-G1 DNA fragmentation, caspase 3/7 activation, and LC3-puncta formation, with wortmannin-mediated rescue indicating that autophagy contributes to cell death, and without detectable induction of reactive oxygen species. This phenotype was accompanied by pronounced disorganization of the actin and tubulin cytoskeletal networks, evidenced by confocal fluorescence microscopy and reduced anisotropy of both networks. Derivative 14 induced less than 5% hemolysis at concentrations up to 1000 μM and was well tolerated in C57BL/6 mice at intraperitoneal doses up to 600 mg/kg, with no mortality or morphological alterations. In silico analyses showed no violations of Lipinski’s rule of five and a topological polar surface area within the range associated with good membrane permeability, while reverse molecular docking pointed to the DNA-binding domains of topoisomerase IIα and IIβ as plausible molecular targets, with binding modes and energies comparable to doxorubicin. Together, these findings establish 14 as a selective and well-tolerated 1,4-naphthoquinone derivative, with a proposed mechanism of action, warranting further preclinical development against OSCC.

item.title: Environment-Aware Deep Learning for Adaptive Dissolved Oxygen Sensing: Resolving the Information Efficiency Paradox in Aquatic Monitoring
item.description:
Abstract
Continuous high-frequency monitoring of dissolved oxygen (DO) faces a fundamental conflict between excessive energy consumption and substantial data redundancy, whereas conventional fixed-frequency sampling risks frequency aliasing and the omission of acute transient ecological events. To resolve this dilemma, a knowledge-guided, seasonally adaptive dynamic sampling strategy coupled with bidirectional long short-term memory (Bi-LSTM) reconstruction is proposed. Validated via long-term datasets from two hydrodynamically distinct Yangtze River stations, this framework yields three principal findings. First, summer precipitation acts as the primary catalyst for acute hypoxic risks (DO < 5.0 mg/L), whereas winter rainfall predominantly drives reaeration, dictating the nonstationary triggers for dynamic sampling. Second, optimal data decimation exhibits pronounced spatial heterogeneity governed by site-specific environmental buffering capacities; high-fidelity reconstruction requires merely 22.99% data retention at the hydrodynamically stable Nanjinguan mainstream. Third, a counterintuitive information efficiency paradox is mathematically proven at the highly volatile Chenglingji lake outlet: the dynamic strategy (utilizing 50.23% of data) achieves a Kling-Gupta efficiency (KGE) of 0.969, vastly outperforming the uncompressed 100% full-data baseline (KGE = 0.797). This confirms that environmentally triggered sparse sampling intrinsically functions as an adaptive nonlinear filter, actively stripping stochastic environmental noise to prevent algorithmic overfitting. Ultimately, integrating physical priors into data acquisition resolves the energy-fidelity trade-off, establishing a highly resilient, low-power architectural foundation for autonomous basin-scale aquatic monitoring networks under escalating climatic extremes.

item.title: Responses of Fibroblasts, Mesenchymal Stem Cells, and Macrophages after Irradiation with Proton and Silver Ion Emission Guns under Atmospheric Pressure
item.description:
Abstract
Various approaches have been developed to regulate cell growth using physiological or physical stimuli. In this study, we focused on ion implantation technology, which has the potential to deliver both types of stimuli. We developed an ion gun capable of releasing protons or silver ions (Ag+) under atmospheric pressure conditions and used it to irradiate mouse fibroblasts (NIH3T3), mouse mesenchymal stem cells (KUSA-A1), and mouse macrophages (RAW264), evaluating their respective responses. Cell viability decreased with increasing doses of ions emitted from the proton gun. Conversely, high doses of ions emitted from the Ag+ gun reduced the metabolic activity of all the cell types, but low doses enhanced that of RAW264 cells. Thus, the effects varied among ion species, even at nearly equivalent doses, indicating distinct cellular responses depending on the ion provided by the guns. Evaluation of osteogenic differentiation after irradiation with a proton gun in KUSA-A1 cells revealed that low doses of ions emitted from the proton gun promoted alkaline phosphatase activity, while high doses inhibited it. This biphasic response suggests that changes in intracellular pH and energy transfer may contribute to the observed response, warranting further investigations.

item.title: Experimental Study on the Synthesis of Molybdenum Disulfide Quantum Dots by Ultrasonic, Solvent-Thermal, and Atmospheric Plasma-Assisted Exfoliation
item.description:
Abstract
Molybdenum disulfide quantum dots (MoS2 QDs) were synthesized using ultrasonic (US), solvent-thermal (ST), and atmospheric plasma-assisted (PA) top-down exfoliation. Energy analysis shows PA exfoliation is remarkably more energy-efficient and faster due to direct plasma-precursor contact. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM) indicated average particle sizes of 4.95 nm (ST), 5.59 nm (US), and 8.69 nm (PA). All samples exhibited strong UV-blue and broad red-to-NIR absorption. The QDs displayed excitation-dependent photoluminescence, with PA samples showing twice the emission intensity of US and ST versions. Across all methods, functional performance was comparable: an 808 nm laser-induced photothermal heating in water to 47 °C within 5 min, while UV irradiation triggered >50% methyl orange photocatalytic degradation within 40 min. This indicates that functional behavior is inherently governed by the QDs rather than the synthesis route. Consequently, highly efficient PA exfoliation offers a promising, scalable pathway for producing multifunctional MoS2 QDs.

item.title: Developing a Quantum Physics-Inspired Machine Learning Model for Partition Coefficient Prediction and Comparing Its Performance with Empirical Descriptors and Molecular Graph-Based Models
item.description:
Abstract
Predicting the partition coefficient (logP) is critical in pharmaceutical research for assessing the bioavailability of small molecules. We present a novel quantum physics-inspired machine learning model (QM-ML) for predicting logP and compare its performance with an empirical descriptor-based model and a graph neural network (GNN) model. For all the models investigated, feature selection was conducted to refine the high-dimensional descriptor space and identify critical determinants of lipophilicity or logP. Quantum mechanical descriptors, in particular frontier orbital energies derived, such as chemical potential, hardness, electrophilicity, electronegativity, and dipole moment, transfer energy, and quantum mechanical polar surface area (QMPSA), were extracted to construct QM-ML mod. The results indicate that the hybrid model achieved the highest predictive accuracy, yielding an R2 of 0.9248, a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.3511, and a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.4981. The ExtraTrees regressor, utilizing empirical classical Mordred descriptors, demonstrated comparable performance with an R2 of 0.9141. While models relying exclusively on frontier orbital energies showed limited accuracy (R2 = 0.4349), the inclusion of explicit solvation energy (ΔG) and QMPSA significantly improved the physics-based model performance (R2 = 0.8132). The DeepChem-based GCN model also achieved an R2 of 0.8936. Notably, the explainability analysis showed that certain QM descriptors, such as solvation energy (ΔG) and non-polar QMPSA, contributed significantly to the model performance. The hybrid model outperformed all the physics-based and baseline Mordred models with large-scale descriptor sets and showed the importance of certain QM descriptors, such as solvation transfer energy and QM-PSA. These findings highlight the potential of a hybrid data-driven model involving physics-based descriptors to capture complex molecular interactions and underscore the importance of targeted feature engineering in quantitative structure–property relationship modeling.

item.title: Integrated Whole-Cell Phage Display and Machine Learning Identify Candidate Targeting Ligands in KRAS-Defined Lung Cancer Contexts
item.description:
Abstract
Phage display can identify ligands that target distinctive cell surface phenotypes, but selection outputs are often complex and difficult to interpret. Here, we developed an integrated workflow combining phage display biopanning, next-generation sequencing (NGS), machine learning (ML), and flow cytometry to discover short peptide binders associated with genotype-defined cancer contexts. Phage display was performed on lung cancer cell lines representing KRAS wild-type (WT), G12C, G12D, and G12V backgrounds, and experimental outputs were used to train a multimodal probabilistic model. From the resulting model-generated candidates, 98 nonredundant heptapeptides were selected for synthesis, and 88 were successfully solubilized and tested experimentally. Flow cytometry validation revealed heterogeneous binding behaviors, including broad pan-cellular binders and candidates with mutant-vs-WT binding preference. Extended dose–response profiling and normal-cell counter-screening enabled prioritization based on binding magnitude, curve behavior, normal-cell reactivity, and sequence developability. Overall, this study shows how whole-cell selection data sets can be analyzed computationally and experimentally to identify and prioritize peptide candidates for targeting strategies.

item.title: Bismuth-Catalyzed Multifunctional Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) Composites with Tunable Thermomechanical Properties for Scalable Manufacturing
item.description:
Abstract
Bismuth-catalyzed silicone systems have recently emerged as promising eco-friendly alternatives to conventional tin- and platinum-based catalysts; however, their behavior in highly filled, scalable composite formulations remains insufficiently understood. In this work, multifunctional polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) composites were developed using a bismuth carboxylate catalyst and two structurally distinct inorganic fillers, perlite and hollow glass microspheres (GMBs), to systematically investigate structure–processing–property relationships and enable tunable thermomechanical performance. Rheological analysis revealed that filler incorporation significantly alters curing behavior, with gelation temperatures increasing from ∼105 °C for neat PDMS to ∼155 °C (+50 °C) for 40 wt % perlite and ∼162 °C (+57 °C) for 40 wt % GMBs, enabling extended processing windows critical for scalable manufacturing. Thermomechanical characterization demonstrated that filler type, through its morphology, intrinsic density, and resulting volume fraction, governs property evolution. Perlite enhanced through-thickness thermal conductivity by up to 42% (0.193 to 0.274 W·m–1·K–1), whereas GMBs reduced thermal conductivity by 47% (to 0.102 W·m–1·K–1), enabling bidirectional thermal transport tuning within a single material platform. Significant reductions in coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) were achieved, reaching 43% (perlite) and 74% (GMBs), while density decreased to <0.65 g·cm–3 for GMB-filled systems, highlighting lightweighting potential. Mechanical performance was substantially improved, with compressive modulus increasing by 339% for perlite-filled composites and up to 1889% for GMB-filled systems, alongside a ∼255% (∼3.6×) higher compressive strength than the perlite-filled composite at the highest filler content. Importantly, the bismuth-catalyzed PDMS formulations exhibited robust scalability, demonstrated through successful sheet molding compound (SMC) processing and compression molding of kilogram-scale, fiber-reinforced composite structures with excellent dimensional stability and flame resistance. These results establish bismuth-catalyzed PDMS composites as a versatile, environmentally benign materials platform with tailorable properties. The findings provide critical insights into filler–matrix–cure interactions and offer a pathway toward the design of next-generation silicone composites for thermal management, lightweight structures, building materials, and large-scale industrial manufacturing.

item.title: Co 2 (OH) 3 Cl/Nb 2 CT x : Advanced Composite Electrodes for High-Performance Aqueous Asymmetric Supercapacitors
item.description:
Abstract
Cobalt hydroxy chloride-based mixed anionic frameworks are attracting attention as supercapacitor electrode materials because of their high theoretical capacity and enhanced redox-active cobalt centers with increased interlayer spacing. on the other hand, Nb2CTx MXene provides conductive, hydrophilic, multivalent Nb that improves electronic transport and maintains good structural stability during electrochemical reactions. In this work, Co2(OH)3Cl/Nb2CTx composites containing 1, 3, and 5 wt % Nb2CTx relative to the mass of Co2(OH)3Cl were synthesized. Further, the specific electrochemical characteristics of the as-prepared composite and bare sample were evaluated using a three-electrode configuration. We fabricated asymmetric supercapacitors using the as-prepared materials as the positive electrode and activated carbon as the negative electrode, with PVA–KOH gel as the electrolyte. The asymmetric supercapacitor fabricated using CN-1 delivered a specific capacity of 158.81 C g–1 at 1 A g–1 and showed a maximum specific energy of 35.29 Wh kg–1 at a specific power of 1.6 kW kg–1. The composite electrode-based device showed an enhanced cycle life of up to 20,000 cycles, with 76.7% capacitance retention and a Coulombic efficiency of around 99%. In contrast, the bare Co2(OH)3Cl-based device retained about 50.6% capacitance after 20,000 cycles. Thus, the optimistic Co2(OH)3Cl/Nb2CTx composites are a potential positive electrode for high-performance supercapacitor applications.

item.title: Taguchi L8 Optimization of Processing Conditions in Designing a Functional Food Product: An Antioxidant-Rich Tomato Soup with Preserved Melatonin-Serotonin- l -Tryptophan Synergy
item.description:
Abstract
The indoleamine antioxidant triad (melatonin, serotonin, and l-tryptophan) displayed in vivo bioavailabilities in rat models when delivered through a tomato-based soup. The present study focuses on the development of this antioxidant-rich tomato-based soup (with preserved antioxidant synergy) through rigorous optimization of processing conditions and comprehensive physicochemical characterization of the finished product, including proximate composition and rheological properties. A Taguchi L8 (eight experimental combinations) orthogonal experimental design was employed to investigate the effects of processing temperature (50–60 °C), guar gum concentration (0.25–0.35%), and processing time (8–10 min) on indoleamine retention and antioxidant synergy effect (SE). Signal-to-noise ratio analysis (larger-the-better criterion) indicated that processing time exerted the most significant influence on indoleamine stability (F = 227.5 for melatonin; F = 171.1 for serotonin; p < 0.05); whereas, temperature and guar gum concentration showed comparatively lesser effects. The optimized processing conditions─processing temperature of 60 °C, addition of 0.35% guar gum, and processing time of 8 min─resulted in maximum retention of melatonin (6.85 μg g–1 dwb), serotonin (17.12 μg g–1 dwb), and l-tryptophan (22.43 μg g–1 dwb) in the designer tomato soup. The same also demonstrated effective preservation of indoleamine stability and antioxidant synergy (SE value 1.01).

item.title: Machine Learning-Driven Comparative Prediction of Compressive Strength in True Geopolymer and Hybrid Alkali-Activated Cement Systems
item.description:
Abstract
Ordinary Portland cement (OPC) production accounts for approximately 7–8% of global CO2 emissions, motivating the development of sustainable binders such as metakaolin-based geopolymers and hybrid alkali-activated cements (AACs). However, accurate prediction of compressive strength in these systems remains challenging because of nonlinear interactions among precursor composition, activator chemistry, water-related parameters, and curing conditions. This study develops a reliability-oriented machine-learning framework using literature-derived datasets comprising 223 metakaolin-based geopolymer mixtures and 262 hybrid AAC mixtures. Five tree-based ensemble algorithms were evaluated using five-fold GroupKFold validation, with literature source used as the grouping variable to reduce the risk of study-level information leakage. The framework further incorporated fold-wise hyperparameter optimization, inverse-frequency sample weighting during model fitting, source-wise sensitivity analysis, and leave-one-source-out evaluation. Under grouped internal validation, CatBoost achieved the best performance for the metakaolin-based geopolymer dataset (R2 = 0.8211 ± 0.1275, RMSE = 5.773 ± 2.333 MPa, MAE = 4.131 ± 1.543 MPa), whereas Gradient Boosting performed best for the hybrid AAC dataset (R2 = 0.8876 ± 0.0708, RMSE = 3.333 ± 1.181 MPa, MAE = 2.366 ± 0.737 MPa). TreeSHAP analysis revealed distinct model-derived feature associations: hybrid AAC predictions were most strongly associated with GGBFS content, followed by activator- and curing-related variables, whereas metakaolin-based geopolymer predictions were most strongly associated with the H2O/Na2O ratio, aggregate proportion, activator chemistry, and curing conditions. These SHAP-derived patterns represent statistical associations learned by the models rather than direct evidence of physical causation or reaction mechanisms. Overall, the proposed framework provides a transparent approach for preliminary compressive-strength screening and experimental prioritization of sustainable alkali-activated binders.

item.title: Balancing Carbon Percolation and MnO 2 Pseudocapacitance in a Few-Layer Graphite/Carbon Black Waterborne Ink for Screen-Printed Planar Microsupercapacitors
item.description:
Abstract
Waterborne conductive inks for screen-printed planar microsupercapacitors (MSCs) must reconcile low-cost processing, print fidelity, electronic conduction, and electrochemical activity. Graphite/carbon black (CB) networks provide scalable conduction but limited charge storage, whereas excessive manganese dioxide (MnO2) can disrupt electron and ion pathways. Here, we identify a practical composition window, within the tested range, for a ternary few-layer graphite (F-GT)/CB/MnO2 ink prepared by high-speed dispersion and planetary ball milling. F-GT forms the long-range conductive scaffold, CB bridges interflake junctions, and MnO2 supplies pseudocapacitive sites without dominating the percolated carbon network. The optimized ink exhibited shear-thinning behavior and reproduced fine patterns on paper and PET. At an F-GT/CB/MnO2 mass ratio of 5:1:3, screen-printed MSCs with a PVA/LiCl gel electrolyte delivered 19.7 mF cm–2 and 9.95 F cm–3 and 1.34 F g–1 at 0.05 mA cm–2 and 2.73 μWh cm–2 at 0.025 mW cm–2. The devices retained 83.7% of their capacitance after 5000 charge–discharge cycles and 90.5% after 1000 bending cycles. Three series-connected devices operated at 3 V and powered a green light-emitting diode. These results show how MnO2 loading can add oxide-based charge storage while preserving a low-cost graphite-derived conductive framework for flexible printed energy storage.

item.title: Performance and Degradation Behavior of Coconut and Sisal Fibers Exposed to Alkaline Solutions and Embedded in Concrete Matrices
item.description:
Abstract
The use of natural lignocellulosic fibers as reinforcement in cementitious materials has attracted increasing interest because of their low environmental impact, renewability, and wide availability. However, the long-term durability of these fibers under highly alkaline conditions remains a major limitation for their application in cement-based composites. This study investigates the degradation behavior and performance of coconut and sisal fibers, under untreated and alkali-treated conditions, exposed to alkaline solutions and incorporated into concretes produced with two Portland cement types (PC V and PC IV). The experimental program included total organic carbon (TOC) analysis, gravimetric degradation tests under cyclic immersion conditions, Fourier transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and compressive strength tests of fiber-reinforced concretes. The results demonstrated that alkalinity is the main factor governing fiber degradation, promoting the dissolution of hemicellulose and lignin, cellulose depolymerization, and progressive microstructural deterioration. TOC analysis revealed substantially higher organic matter release under alkaline exposure compared with thermal treatment alone, confirming the strong susceptibility of lignocellulosic components to alkaline attack. Sisal fibers exhibited higher initial degradation due to their elevated cellulose content and lower lignin fraction, whereas coconut fibers showed a greater chemical stability. Alkali treatment reduced the mass loss during degradation cycles, particularly for sisal fibers, indicating partial stabilization through the removal of alkali-sensitive amorphous constituents. FT-IR analyses showed that cellulose-related bands near 1400 cm–1 and 1028–1052 cm–1 are sensitive indicators of alkaline degradation, especially for sisal fibers exposed to the simulated pore solution. SEM observations confirmed significant surface deterioration, microfibril separation, and increased roughness after alkaline exposure with treated fibers generally exhibiting lower structural damage than untreated fibers. In the concrete mixtures, coconut fibers demonstrated superior compatibility with both cement matrices, maintaining compressive strength values close to those of the reference concrete. Conversely, sisal fibers caused significant reductions in compressive strength, despite their intrinsically higher tensile properties, indicating that chemical durability and fiber stability govern composite performance more strongly than the isolated fiber strength. The results further indicate that the moderate reduction in alkalinity provided by PC IV cement is insufficient to prevent the degradation of cellulose-rich fibers. Overall, the study demonstrates that fiber composition and chemical stability are critical factors controlling the performance of natural fiber-reinforced cementitious composites, highlighting coconut fibers as a more promising alternative for applications in alkaline environments.

item.title: Phenolate-Mediated Structural Evolution of Lignin toward Hard Carbon Anodes for Sodium-Ion Batteries
item.description:
Abstract
Hard carbon (HC) anodes are typically described in terms of their final structure. However, this structure is influenced by multiple competing factors, and precursor-level chemical interactions can play an important role in directing its eventual evolution. Here, metal coordination is used to direct lignin precursor organization and control the evolution of lignin-derived HCs. Magnesium gluconate (MgGlu2) introduced into alkaline lignin promotes selective Mg2+ coordination with oxygen-containing functional groups, enabling reorganization of the lignin network prior to carbonization. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations show a thermodynamic preference of Mg2+ for phenolate (Ph–)-rich environments over gluconate ligands and β–O–4 linkages, consistent with the formation of cross-linked precursor configurations. This coordination is preserved during freeze-drying and translates into a distinct carbon microstructure upon pyrolysis. The resulting carbon exhibits a more accessible pore structure and improved cycling stability, retaining 93.6% of its post-solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) capacity after 400 cycles, compared to 8.7% for the pristine counterpart. These results demonstrate that phenolate-directed Mg2+ coordination governs precursor organization and contributes to the structural stability of lignin-derived HCs. More broadly, this work establishes precursor-level coordination as a route to control structure–performance relationships in HC anodes.

item.title: Toll-Like Receptors in Mycoplasma Infections: Immunopathogenesis, Cheminformatics, and Machine Learning-Based Insights into TLR-Targeted Therapeutics
item.description:
Abstract
Mycoplasma species are the minimal-genome pathogens that elicit complex host immune responses involving both protective and pathogenic inflammation. Toll-like receptors (TLRs) are pivotal components of the immune system, recognizing pathogen-associated molecular patterns and damage-associated molecular patterns to initiate immune responses. TLRs recognize Mycoplasma-derived lipoproteins, glycolipids, and CpG-rich DNA motifs, initiating NF-κB and MAPK signaling cascades. While these pathways are indispensable for microbial clearance, their dysregulation contributes to chronic inflammation, autoimmunity, and tissue damage. Consequently, selective modulation of TLR signaling has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy for restoring immune homeostasis. In this study, we summarized the recent advances in delineating the molecular crosstalk between TLRs and Mycoplasma, emphasizing the distinct roles of TLRs in pathogen recognition and immunopathology. In parallel, it integrates a cheminformatics-based analysis of TLR inhibitory ligands retrieved from the ChEMBL database, encompassing over 230 compounds across TLR1–5. Multivariate visualization techniques such as principal component analysis (PCA), uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP), and t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) were employed to map the chemical space and reveal receptor-specific clustering patterns. The analysis identified TLR2 and TLR4 inhibitors as occupying distinct but overlapping chemical regions, characterized by higher molecular weight, lipophilicity, and structural complexity. Correlation and similarity mapping further highlighted scaffold conservation among active ligands, providing a quantitative foundation for rational drug design and structure–activity modeling. Furthermore, we explore how machine learning (ML) and computational modeling are reshaping TLR-targeted drug discovery. ML-driven frameworks facilitate ligand prediction, virtual screening, and structure–activity optimization through deep docking and transformer-based scoring models. Integrative ML approaches also extend beyond ligand discovery to encompass multiomics data integration, biomarker identification, and predictive modeling of host–pathogen interactions and immune responses. By bridging immunological insight with cheminformatics and ML-based analytics, this article outlines a multidisciplinary roadmap for precision immunomodulation in Mycoplasma-associated diseases. The convergence of experimental pharmacology and computational intelligence holds the potential to accelerate the discovery of next-generation TLR-targeted therapeutics, advancing personalized strategies for immune regulation and infection control.

item.title: Molecular Engineering of Sarcosine Oxidase and Horseradish Peroxidase: Impact of Lysine Accessibility on Covalent Bioconjugation and Bioelectrocatalysis
item.description:
Abstract
Sarcosine has emerged as a critical biomarker for the early diagnosis of prostate cancer, necessitating the development of highly sensitive and simplified electrochemical detection methods. While the bioconjugation of enzymes offers a pathway toward enhanced bioelectronic performance, biosensors based on bioconjugated sarcosine oxidase remain largely unexplored. In this study, we used a synthesized redox mediator, N-(ferrocenylmethyl)-6-aminohexanoic acid, featuring an extended spacer arm designed to decrease the tunneling distance between the enzyme cofactor and the electrode surface. Sarcosine oxidase and horseradish peroxidase were subjected to bioconjugation via carbodiimide-mediated coupling. The resulting bioconjugates were characterized by cyclic voltammetry, diffusion-kinetic analysis, and high-resolution mass spectrometry following tryptic and peptic digestion. Furthermore, an in silico structural analysis was employed to correlate lysine solvent-accessible surface area with conjugation efficiency. Based on these bioconjugates, a sarcosine biosensor was constructed and tested using human serum as real samples.

item.title: Template-Derived Nickel Oxide Catalysts for Reproducible Oxidative Dehydrogenation of Ethane
item.description:
Abstract
Ethylene, an essential feedstock for many materials, was produced through ethane oxidative dehydrogenation using a template-derived nickel oxide catalyst. A Ni-based metal-organic framework, Ni-BTC, was used as the template, and catalyst preparation was evaluated by varying calcination time, decomposition environment, and preparation timing. These variables were probed to determine the effect on the reproducibility of the nickel oxide catalyst. Samples were characterized using surface area, X-ray diffraction, and thermogravimetric analysis. Findings indicate that template-derived nickel oxide gives reproducible spent-surface-area-normalized ethylene production, with the RSD error minimized to 3.0% compared to 29.0% for the traditional sol–gel preparation method. The best-performing conditions identified in this study were complete air decomposition for 4 h at 400 °C and limited storage time before catalytic testing. Heating the spent catalyst after the reaction provided insight into the effectiveness of the decomposition environments but did not further improve the air-decomposed samples.

item.title: Three Fundamental Challenges in Deep Coal and Gas Outburst: Progress, Controversies, and Future Perspectives
item.description:
Abstract
Coal and gas outburst (CGO) remains one of the most severe dynamic hazards in deep coal mining. Increasing burial depth challenges conventional single-factor criteria. This critical review synthesizes advances in CGO mechanisms reported between 2015 and 2025, focusing on three fundamental challenges: the limited applicability of the 0.74 MPa gas-pressure threshold under deep conditions, the nonmonotonic thermal regulation of gas adsorption–desorption and transport, and the apparent high-storage–low-trigger paradox of tectonically deformed coal (TDC). Comparative assessment of elastic-energy- and adsorbed-gas-dominated theories indicates that deep outbursts are better interpreted as condition-dependent competition among elastic strain energy, gas expansion work, fracture-energy consumption, and dissipative processes. Reported values further show that coal deformation/fracture energy and gas expansion energy can become comparable in magnitude, whereas the fraction of adsorbed-gas energy converted into dynamic work remains highly uncertain.
