item.title: Signal-Analytics Modeling of Fluorescence Maximum Time-to-Detection (TTD + ) for E. coli in Treated Wastewater: A Joint Censoring and Sensor Model Approach Part II
item.description:
Abstract
Water security is a global priority and relies on reliable microbiological monitoring in treated effluents. In this work, we investigate a sensor-analytics component of Escherichia coli (E. coli) monitoring in treated wastewater through fluorescence time courses acquired with a miniaturized, Internet of Things-enabled incubation platform, named the Optical Bacterial Growth Sensor–Fluorescence Detector. The signal arises from hydrolysis of a β-d-glucuronide substrate mediated by E. coli-expressed β-glucuronidase activity, yielding characteristic kinetic profiles over time. Our primary target is the extraction and probabilistic modeling of the upper time-to-detection, TTD+, an operational timing feature of the recorded fluorescence response. In practical terms, TTD+ retrospectively identifies the onset of the upper stable signal region under the adopted criterion, providing a timing summary for assay duration planning. To model this time-domain boundary, we adopt the Joint Censoring and Sensor Model Approach (JCSMA) and further extend it by deriving analytical expressions for ordinary moments and entropy measures, including Rényi and Shannon entropies. The empirical comparison favors JCSMA within the evaluated model set, while simulation characterizes the sampling behavior of selected statistics under the fitted model. The resulting probabilities and quantiles provide summaries for assay duration planning under the adopted conditions. The study does not evaluate analytical figures of merit for E. coli quantification or the association between TTD+ and reference most probable number values.

item.title: Wettability-Controlled Hydrophobic Deep Eutectic Solvents for Sustainable and Rapid Removal of Hexavalent Chromium
item.description:
Abstract
The removal of hexavalent chromium (Cr(VI)) from industrial effluents remains challenging for conventional solvent extraction systems due to sluggish mass transfer, limited extraction capacity, and the inherent toxicity of volatile organic compounds. Here, we report a wettability-modulated strategy to overcome these limitations using hydrophobic deep eutectic solvents (HDESs) based on quaternary ammonium salts and fatty acids. By correlating the contact angle, viscosity, and hydrogen-bonding network with extraction performance, we identify the optimized HDES, [N8881][Br]-OA(1:2), which exhibits a remarkably low viscosity (147.6 cP at 298.2 K) and a favorable contact angle (34.4°), enabling rapid interfacial anion exchange. This extractant achieves a single-stage Cr(VI) recovery exceeding 99% within only 10 min at an initial concentration of 500 mg·L–1 under an oil-to-water ratio of 1:50. Mechanistic investigations confirm a reversible Br–/HCrO4– anion-exchange pathway, while thermodynamic analysis reveals an endothermic and entropy-driven process. Notably, the HDES maintains over 95% extraction efficiency after 12 successive regeneration cycles without structural degradation and outperforms the benchmark solvent methyl isobutyl ketone (MIBK) by a factor of 12. This work demonstrates that tailoring the wettability of HDESs provides a green, sustainable, and industrially viable platform for the ultrafast decontamination of Cr(VI)-laden wastewater, with significant potential for scalable water treatment applications.

item.title: An Experimental Study on the Quantitative Mesoscopic Roughness Characteristics of Rock Using the Size Reduction Method
item.description:
Abstract
The development of emerging clean energy technologies, including CO2 geological sequestration, enhanced geothermal systems (EGS), and underground hydrogen storage, faces a critical scientific and engineering challenge: the accurate characterization of complex fracture morphology in subsurface rock formations. Accurate quantification of fracture morphology is a fundamental prerequisite for engineering design and numerical simulation. However, current methodologies for fracture characterization often fail to effectively distinguish between detailed features such as fracture orientation and surface roughness, leading to imprecise characterization results that directly impact the quality of engineering implementation. This study introduces an innovative theoretical framework─the size reduction method─which isolates detailed roughness from surface tortuosity. Additionally, a novel detailed roughness index, Ra-r, is proposed to complement this method. Utilizing this advanced approach, the research conducts a comprehensive comparison of surface roughness across various fracture types: different regions within a single fracture, natural versus hydraulic fractures within the same specimen, fractures of identical lithology, and fractures of differing lithologies. The findings reveal several critical insights: First, within a single fracture, the roughness at turning positions is significantly lower than that in positions with a unidirectional trend, approximately 31.9% of the latter. Second, hydraulic fractures in carbonatite specimens exhibit higher roughness compared to natural fractures. Third, the presence of quartz mineral fillings reduces the roughness of carbonatite hydraulic fractures to 69.4%. Lastly, a comparison between carbonatite and shale fractures indicates that the roughness of shale hydraulic fractures is about 50.6% of that of carbonatite, while the roughness of natural fractures in shale is approximately 51.4% of that of carbonatite. This research offers significant contributions to the theoretical understanding and practical applications of fracture flow dynamics, providing a robust foundation for future studies and industrial implementations in the field of resource extraction.

item.title: Thermodynamically Constrained Deep Learning for Hydrogen Sorption Prediction: Overcoming Classical Isotherm Generalization Failure through Physics-Informed Cross-Lithology Transferability
item.description:
Abstract
Accurate prediction of hydrogen sorption in fine-grained geological materials is essential for subsurface energy systems. While classical isotherm models describe individual samples effectively, they fail to generalize across heterogeneous populations, with R2 dropping from 0.80–0.90 for single-sample fits to 0.09–0.38 for aggregated data sets. This limitation demonstrates that predictive models must explicitly account for intrinsic material properties and fundamental physical constraints. We present a thermodynamics-informed, physics-regularized neural network framework designed to improve predictive accuracy and cross-lithology generalization. The framework integrates three core components: a seven-category physics-informed feature engineering scheme generating 62 thermodynamically meaningful descriptors, a multiterm loss function enforcing saturation limits and monotonic pressure responses through penalty-weighted terms, and an architecture-diverse ten-member ensemble with post hoc temperature-scaling calibration to provide reliable uncertainty estimates. Van’t Hoff temperature dependence is incorporated through thermodynamic feature engineering, with all model components integrated within a three-phase curriculum training strategy that progressively introduces physical regularization. On a random-split holdout set, the framework achieves R2 = 0.9544, RMSE = 0.0484 mmol/g, and MAE = 0.0231 mmol/g, with a 98.6% monotonicity satisfaction rate and zero nonphysical negative predictions. Because random splits primarily evaluate interpolation within the observed distribution, we prioritize leave-one-lithology-out (LOLO) validation to assess physical generalization under distribution shift. When entire geological classes are withheld from training, the framework retains R2 = 0.723 for coal and 0.794 for shale, outperforming a well-tuned random forest baseline (R2 = 0.631 and 0.712, respectively) by 14.6% and 11.5%, respectively. These results support the effectiveness of thermodynamic constraints as a generalization scaffold across geological boundaries, providing a practical foundation for evaluating formations whose lithological classes are absent from the training data.

item.title: Comparative HPHC Emission Profiles of Combustible and Alternative Nicotine Products in South Africa: Development of a Relative HPHC Emission Index
item.description:
Abstract
Alternative nicotine and tobacco products are increasingly available in South Africa, yet independent comparative data on their harmful and potentially harmful constituent (HPHC) emission profiles remain limited. The aim of this study was to compare mainstream emissions from an illicit combustible cigarette (Brand X), IQOS ILUMA heated tobacco products (TEREA Amber and TEREA Turquoise), a VEEV Now Ultra Mint disposable electronic nicotine delivery system, and ZYN modern oral nicotine pouches, with the 1R6F reference cigarette included as a combustible benchmark. Combustion-related markers CO, NO and NOx were evaluated in TEREA aerosols under synthetic-air and nitrogen atmospheres, while nine WHO-priority HPHCs were quantified using standardized analytical methods. Emissions were normalized to 100 cm3 of nominal puff volume where applicable. Brand X produced high emissions across the measured HPHC panel, including 4.91 ± 0.28 mg/100 cm3 CO, 248.67 ± 14.55 μg/100 cm3 acetaldehyde, 23.66 ± 2.27 μg/100 cm3 acrolein, 11.33 ± 1.43 μg/100 cm3 formaldehyde, 17.20 ± 0.75 μg/100 cm3 1,3-butadiene and 13.29 ± 1.01 μg/100 cm3 benzene. TEREA aerosols generated CO, NO and NOx concentrations below the BSI PAS 8850:2020 combustion-marker thresholds under both atmospheres, supporting the absence of combustion under the tested conditions. Across the WHO-9 panel, TEREA aerosols showed substantially lower emissions than combustible cigarette smoke, while VEEV showed quantifiable acetaldehyde and formaldehyde at low levels and most other target constituents below detection limits. Nicotine pouches showed a similarly restricted profile. Among TEREA variants, only NNN remained different after Holm adjustment. To integrate the multidimensional HPHC data, a Relative HPHC Emission Index (RHEI) was developed by normalizing each constituent to the highest emission among VEEV, TEREA Turquoise and Brand X and combining the nine constituent scores using equal weighting. The RHEI showed clear separation among the three products, with Brand X having the highest relative HPHC emission profile, TEREA Turquoise an intermediate profile, and VEEV the lowest. These findings provide an analytical basis for product-specific evaluation and surveillance of nicotine products in South Africa.

item.title: Effect of In Mole Fraction on Gamma Ray Shielding Properties of In x Al 1–x As Material
item.description:
Abstract
The gamma-ray shielding performance of InxAl1–xAs with different In mole fractions was systematically investigated via the Phy-X/PSD. Key shielding parameters including mass attenuation coefficient (MAC), linear attenuation coefficient (LAC), half-value layer (HVL), tenth-value layer (TVL), mean free path (MFP), atomic cross-section (ACS), electronic cross-section (ECS), effective atomic number (Zeff), effective electron density (Neff), effective conductivity (Ceff), R-value, and equivalent atomic number (Zeq) were calculated over the energy range of 0.015–15 MeV. The results demonstrate that the MAC, LAC, ACS, ECS, Zeff, Ceff, and Zeq values increase with a rising In mole fraction, with In0.8Al0.2As exhibiting the highest values among the studied samples, alongside lower HVL, TVL, and MFP values. At equivalent photon energies, a linear correlation was observed between HVL, TVL, and MFP and the In mole fraction as x increased from 0.25 to 0.8. To quantify the composition-driven enhancement, a comprehensive shielding performance index (ICSP) was defined, and In0.8Al0.2As showed up to a 369% improvement at 0.1 MeV relative to In0.25Al0.75As.These findings suggest that increasing In content effectively enhances the gamma-ray attenuation capability of InAlAs materials. Furthermore, the observed linear relationships between shielding parameters and composition enable the prediction and optimization of shielding performance through compositional tuning, providing a theoretical foundation for the compositional design of III–V compound semiconductors in radiation shielding applications.

item.title: Energy-Efficient and Low-Temperature Gaseous Concentration Swing Adsorption (GCSA)-Based Regeneration Method Utilizing Hydrogen Sweep for Direct Air Capture
item.description:
Abstract
Solid sorbent-based direct air capture (DAC) is a promising pathway for durable carbon dioxide removal (CDR), but large-scale deployment remains constrained by sorbent degradation and the high cost and energy associated with temperature-vacuum swing adsorption (TVSA). Here, we introduce a hydrogen (H2)-enabled gaseous concentration swing adsorption (GCSA) process that eliminates vacuum and enables regeneration at 35–70 °C using a closed-loop H2 sweep with a commercial amine sorbent. By lowering the CO2 partial pressure under reducing conditions near ambient pressure, H2-GCSA achieves effective regeneration with reduced thermal severity and suppressed oxidative degradation. Accelerated testing between 65 and 95 °C under oxidative and anaerobic environments demonstrates superior sorbent stability over 100 h under oxygen-free conditions. A process-integrated techno-economic analysis for a 100,000 tCO2/yr modular DAC plant, utilizing a total of less than 8.5 tons of H2 and incorporating downstream H2/CO2 separation via pressure swing adsorption (PSA), projects an energy demand of 2.78 GJ/tCO2 (775 KWh/tCO2) and a capture cost of 81 USD/tCO2, representing a 2–3× lower capital cost and 1.5–4× lower energy demand relative to TVSA. Further process integration using low-grade waste heat and PSA elimination reduces the energy demand to 0.85 GJ/tCO2 (235 KWh/tCO2), with projected costs approaching 31 USD/tCO2. Sensitivity analysis indicates that the sorbent cost below 95 USD/kg enables DAC below 100 USD/tCO2. Collectively, these results demonstrate that H2 sweep-mediated GCSA offers a scalable, lower-energy alternative to vacuum-driven (TVSA) regeneration on a wide range of sorbents, eliminating the sorbent material development risks and addressing a central bottleneck in solid-sorbent DAC.

item.title: Machine Learning-Assisted Optimization of Surfactin Titer Produced by Bacillus subtilis MTCC 2423 from Minimum Fermentation Data with Experimental Validation
item.description:
Abstract
Optimizing surfactin production from a wild-type Bacillus sp., is challenging due to complex microbial growth kinetics, nonlinear interactions among process variables, and the lack of mechanistic models to describe surfactin production. Therefore, the present study develops data-driven machine learning models to optimize surfactin production from Bacillus subtilis MTCC 2423 under limited fermentation data. First, 25 batch fermentation experiments were performed to obtain surfactin titers under varied conditions of temperature, agitation speed, and inoculum volume, generated using a central composite design (CCD) integrated with maximin Latin hypercube sampling (LHS). Subsequently, machine learning models, viz, multivariable least-squares regression (MVLSR), Gaussian process regression (GPR), support vector regression (SVR), and random forest (RF), were trained and evaluated using the nested leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) to achieve robust prediction of the surfactin titer. Hyperparameter tuning of the models was performed using a genetic algorithm (GA) and grid search. Both the GPR and SVR outperformed the other models and demonstrated comparable predictive performance on the unseen data, producing the LOOCV R2 of 0.89 and 0.86, and LOOCV RMSE of 0.6 and 0.67, respectively. Subsequently, the mean response surface plots were constructed using the GPR model to illustrate the effects of nonlinear interactions among the input features on the surfactin titer. Finally, a GPR-based constrained optimization yielded an optimal surfactin titer of 5.72 g L–1, compared to the base-case value of 1.49 g L–1, while identifying the optimal process variables. The data-driven optimization results closely agreed with the experimentally validated surfactin titer of 5.75 ± 0.09 g L–1, demonstrating high model reliability and predictive accuracy. Our experimental design approach, integrated with machine-learning-driven optimization using limited experimental data, can be adopted across various bioprocess sectors to achieve substantial improvements in surfactin titer.

item.title: Characterization of Extracellular Vesicles from Attenuated and Virulent Leishmania amazonensis Promastigotes Reveals Distinct Proteomic Signatures
item.description:
Abstract
Leishmaniasis is a group of endemic diseases caused by different species of Leishmania. Virulence factors produced by Leishmania can be found in extracellular vesicles (EVs), a heterogeneous group of particles released by cells that are involved in cell-to-cell communication. Herein, we demonstrated that Leishmania amazonensis subjected to three in vivo passages exhibited exacerbated virulence, while prolonged culture resulted in an attenuated profile. The morphological characterization of EVs released by these parasites showed no significant differences. However, proteomic analysis revealed enrichment of proteins associated with proteolysis in EVs released by virulent parasites. In addition, these EVs showed significantly higher proteasome activity compared to EVs from attenuated L. amazonensis promastigotes. Attenuated and virulent parasites incorporated EVs. However, we observed a significant increase in murine macrophage infectivity by virulent parasites following uptake of autologous EVs. Thus, our findings show that L. amazonensis parasites with distinct virulence profiles release EVs with differences in the relative abundance of their protein cargo, which may contribute to the maintenance or enhancement of parasite infectivity.

item.title: Vapor Phase Infiltration of Metal Oxides for Water Treatment Membranes: Potential and Limitations
item.description:
Abstract
Membrane-based water treatment processes are critical for global water security, yet current state-of-the-art polymeric membranes face limitations in mechanical, chemical, and thermal stability. Ceramic membranes, on the other hand, foul less, are easy to clean, and have high modulus values, but they are brittle and less permeable when used as dense membranes. Vapor phase infiltration (VPI) of metal oxides, a derivative of atomic layer deposition (ALD) that transforms organic polymers into organic–inorganic hybrid materials, offers a novel method to modify polymeric membranes and allow them to have the advantages of both polymeric and ceramic membranes. In this review, we combine insights from the use of VPI with polymeric substrates and organic solvent separation membranes to provide our view of the potential and limitations of VPI for enhancing water treatment membranes. We examine how VPI of metal oxides improves the mechanical strength, which is relevant to compaction-resistant reverse osmosis supports, and chemical stability, which could play a role in membrane chlorine and extreme-pH tolerance. We also critically evaluate the associated trade-offs, most notably potential reductions in water permeance arising from the intrinsically lower water permeability of metal oxides. We further identify ion exchange membranes and electrodialysis as especially promising targets, where suppressed water transport is advantageous for ion–ion selectivity. Together, these insights clarify where VPI of metal oxides can most effectively advance emerging membrane-based water treatment technologies.

item.title: Performance Evaluation of CO 2 Huff-n-Puff in Shale Oil Reservoirs: Multiwell Huff-n-Puff and Parameter Optimization
item.description:
Abstract
CO2 huff-n-puff (HnP) is an established enhanced oil recovery (EOR) method for shale oil reservoirs. However, its field-scale implementation in multiwell fractured systems remains challenging because fracture-controlled interwell connectivity can cause operational interference and inefficient CO2 allocation. A field-scale numerical model of the HH shale oil reservoir, incorporating complex natural and hydraulic fracture networks, was constructed and history-matched against field production data, followed by a structured sequential one-factor-at-a-time analysis and descriptive Spearman rank-correlation screening of the associations between operational parameters and performance indicators. Results indicate that, for the calibrated HH reservoir realization, the intragroup synchronized and intergroup asynchronous strategy achieved the highest cumulative incremental oil production among the investigated strategies (9.59 × 104 t), together with a CO2 utilization efficiency of 0.266 t oil/t CO2. This performance was associated with the cross-group pressure contrast observed under the asynchronous operation of the two well groups. Rank-correlation screening indicated that cycle number and cyclic CO2 injection mass showed the strongest associations with oil recovery and CO2 utilization efficiency, respectively, within the investigated cases. Within the investigated ranges and under the experimentally constrained diffusion setting of the calibrated HH reservoir model, 45 days and 450 t/d were identified as the preferred soaking time and injection rate, respectively. Extending the soaking time from 45 to 55 days yielded only marginal improvements, whereas increasing the injection rate from 450 to 600 t/d slightly reduced both incremental oil production and CO2 utilization efficiency. Furthermore, compared with the uniform injection scheme, the differentiated injection scheme maintained a comparable OOIP-based recovery factor (15.97% versus 15.84%) while reducing the cumulative gross CO2 injection mass from 36.0 × 104 to 33.1 × 104 t, corresponding to an 8.1% reduction. The EOR-oriented CO2 utilization efficiency consequently increased from 0.274 to 0.305 t oil/t CO2. Therefore, its principal benefit was the more efficient use of the injected CO2 rather than a substantial increase in ultimate oil recovery. This work provides a field-scale numerical workflow for designing and evaluating coordinated multiwell CO2 HnP operations in fractured shale oil reservoirs.

item.title: Data Characterization and Multi-Plant Data Integration Strategies for Artificial Neural Network Modeling in Palm Oil Refining
item.description:
Abstract
Real-time quality monitoring in palm oil refining is often hindered by laboratory delays, which can be mitigated through the development of Artificial Neural Network (ANN) soft sensors. However, the effectiveness of these models is constrained by the characteristics of available process data. To address this, this study establishes a quantitative framework for assessing data set suitability by analyzing industrial data from three refineries using coefficient of variation (CV) statistics and self-organizing map (SOM) visualizations, with a feedforward neural network (FFN) used as a baseline model. Results show that process variables with CV exceeding 50% consistently yield better FFN performance than those below 50%. An integration strategy between different refineries was introduced to overcome the limitation of single-plant data and improve model performance to above 80% prediction accuracy for FFA content and Red Lovibond color. To test whether this improvement resulted from model capacity rather than data variability. The results further showed that data variability significantly affects model performance rather than model architecture. These findings establish CV as a practical criterion for data set suitability in ANN modeling for palm oil refining, offering an approach other chemical process industries facing similarly low-variation data may adapt.

item.title: Covalent Surface Modification of Polyester Fabric with Carvacrol and Eugenol
item.description:
Abstract
Synthetic fibers such as polyester (PES) are highly valued for their strength and low cost, yet their inherent hydrophobicity and poor dyeability remain significant challenges. To address these limitations sustainably, this study presents a novel surface modification of PES that combines mild lipase-catalyzed hydrolysis to generate reactive surface carboxyl groups, followed by direct esterification with the natural phenolic compounds carvacrol and eugenol. The efficacy of this functionalization was evaluated using FTIR, UV–vis, contact angle, SEM, and thermal analysis. Optimization revealed that a 40 wt % oil concentration provided the optimal balance, achieving effective surface incorporation of 8.3 mmol g–1 of fabric for carvacrol and 6.1 mmol g–1 for eugenol. FTIR, along with 5-cycle wash-fastness tests, indicated the durable formation of covalent ester bonds. The resulting modified fabrics exhibited excellent hydrophilicity (contact angle reduced from 116.17° to 0° with immediate absorption) and significantly enhanced dye diffusion and color fastness matching untreated standards. Additionally, incorporating these terpenes imparted high-value properties, notably reducing flame propagation (remaining length increasing from 2.7 cm to 4.1–4.3 cm) and inhibiting Candida albicans proliferation by 48–90%. These findings highlight a promising, eco-friendly pathway for the durable, covalent functionalization of polyester textiles.

item.title: Laser-Induced Graphene Modified with Gold Nanoparticles for Dengue Biomarker Detection: Toward Portable and Flexible Biosensing Platforms for Early Diagnosis
item.description:
Abstract
Dengue remains a major public health challenge in tropical and subtropical regions, where early detection can support timely clinical management. Nonstructural protein 1 (NS1), released during the acute phase of infection, is an important biomarker for early dengue detection. Here, we report a flexible electrochemical immunosensor based on laser-induced graphene (LIG), a hierarchically porous three-dimensional carbon material produced by laser irradiation of polyimide and functionalized with gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) through a simple electroless deposition process. The incorporation of AuNPs reduced the impedance of the LIG electrode, enhanced interfacial charge transfer, and increased the electrochemically accessible surface area. Structural, morphological, electrochemical, and surface wettability characterizations confirmed the successive modification steps of the sensing platform. The resulting biosensor exhibited a logarithmic response to DENV-2 NS1 over the experimentally evaluated concentration range of 10–1000 ng/mL, with a calculated limit of detection of 3.3 ng/mL. The sensor showed reproducible responses and low cross-reactivity toward Zika virus NS1 under the investigated conditions. These results demonstrate the feasibility of combining porous LIG and AuNPs for electrochemical NS1 detection and provide a basis for the further development of flexible electrochemical biosensors for dengue NS1 detection.

item.title: Enhanced Electrical Output for Triboelectric Nanogenerator Based on Cobalt-Doped Zeolitic Imidazolate Framework as a Multifunctional Filler for Negative Tribolayer
item.description:
Abstract
Developing more efficient triboelectric nanogenerators raises several questions about how to tune the dielectric constant, porosity, and charge-trapping ability of friction layers. Herein, the modification of the standard Ecoflex layer was achieved by the incorporation of pure imidazolate zeolitic frameworks (ZIF-8 and ZIF-67) and modified structures (Cox%/ZIF-8), as a strategy for tuning the dielectric constant of the heterostructure (ZIF/Ecoflex) and the charge transfer rate by progressive incorporation of a cobalt-doping element. As a result, the dielectric constant varied from (2.81 ± 0.28) for pure Ecoflex to (3.29 ± 0.01) for the ZIF-67/Ecoflex composite, while fixed-point Kelvin probe experiments indicate faster charge rearrangement in ZIF-67-based composites. As a consequence of the direct relationship between the transferred charge density and the variation in the dielectric constant of the friction layer, the modification provided by the ZIF incorporation into Ecoflex resulted in an improvement of 58% in the short-circuit current and 170% in the open-circuit voltage measured at 4 Hz, characterizing important findings for cobalt-doping effects in ZIF derivatives applied as a nanofiller in the friction layer for TENGs.

item.title: Gas-Phase Reactivity of AuSiO 3 – Anion Clusters with n-Alkanes (C 1 –C 4 ): Distinguishing Capture, Stabilized Association, and C–H Bond Activation
item.description:
Abstract
The reactivity of heteronuclear gold-silicon oxide cluster anion AuSiO3– toward small alkanes (C1–C4) has been experimentally investigated at room temperature by employing a homemade reflectron time-of-flight mass spectrometer. Experimental results reveal distinct reaction channels for these systems, which produce hydrogen-containing dissociation products (SiO3H–) and associative adducts (AuSiO3CnH2n+2–, n = 1–4). While the total depletion (capture) rate increases with increasing chain length, the branching ratio of dissociation products correspondingly decreases. Density functional theory calculations demonstrate that the two-fold-coordinated gold ion (Au+) anchored on the AuSiO3– cluster proceeds via an oxidative addition mechanism involving homolytic bond cleavage. Both RRKM calculations and MESMER master-equation simulations reveal that for larger alkanes such as C4H10, the rapidly growing density of vibrational states with increasing chain length shifts the competition from product dissociation toward collisional stabilization, thereby favoring associative adduct formation over dissociation pathways─a stark contrast to the behavior observed in the AuSiO3––CH4 reaction. This work provides novel insights into the competition among collisional capture, stabilized association, and C–H bond activation in small-molecule alkanes.

item.title: Large-Area Metasurfaces for Enhanced Fluorescence Imaging
item.description:
Abstract
All-dielectric metasurfaces have been extensively applied to three-dimensional displays, vortex beam generation, beam steering, and luminescence enhancement. However, studies on all-dielectric metasurfaces for enhancing biofluorescence imaging remain relatively scarce. In this study, an anodic aluminum oxide (AAO) template is employed to fabricate a large-area silicon metasurface embedded in PDMS to serve as a fluorescence imaging slide. Under the excitation of the electromagnetic dipole resonance of metasurface, the cells stained with iFluor 555-phalloidin on the metasurface film exhibit a fluorescence enhancement potentially arising from the combined contributions of Purcell-related radiative decay-rate modification, local excitation-field enhancement, and changes in fluorescence collection efficiency, substantially improving the fluorescence imaging quality. The experimental results demonstrate that when the silicon metasurface embedded in PDMS serves as a fluorescence imaging slide, the fluorescence imaging intensity is enhanced by a factor of approximately 3.38. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of large-area all-dielectric metasurfaces fabricated via the AAO template method for enhanced fluorescence imaging. This finding broadens the scope of all-dielectric metasurfaces with large area for biomedical fluorescence imaging.

item.title: Charge-Induced Conductance Modulation and Capacitive Properties of Two-Layer–like 2γ-In 2 Se 3 : Insights from Density Functional Theory
item.description:
Abstract
We investigate the field- and charge-driven electronic instabilities in two-layer–like 2γ-In2Se3 with implications for charge-induced conductance modulation. Using density functional theory, we examine the effects of an external electric field and charge doping on the electronic structure. While the electric field primarily redistributes charge carriers, charge doping directly controls the occupation of the Mexican-hat–like states and the associated van Hove singularity near the valence-band edge. The charge-controlled occupation of the Mexican-hat-like states governs both spin polarization and in-plane conductivity, thereby providing a microscopic mechanism for conductance modulation. This work suggests that two-layer-like 2γ-In2Se3 may provide a useful platform for exploring field- and charge-tunable electronic responses relevant to nanoelectronics.

item.title: Extraction of Calcium from Steel Slag via Low-Temperature Chlorination Roasting and Water Leaching for the Preparation of CaCO 3
item.description:
Abstract
This paper proposes a novel coupled process of “low-temperature chlorination roasting with NH4Cl─water leaching for calcium separation─carbonation precipitation” to achieve selective recovery and utilization of calcium from steel slag. Thermodynamic calculations indicate the presence of two reaction pathways in the system: solid–solid chlorination and gas–solid chlorination mediated by HCl. Among these, the gas-phase chlorination reaction exhibits a stronger thermodynamic spontaneity. Phase analysis of the raw steel slag shows that calcium is primarily found in the phases of Ca2SiO4, Ca2Fe2O5, and Al14Ca12O33, with a positive correlation to the contents of silicon, iron, and aluminum. The roasting temperature and holding time have been identified as the core factors affecting the calcium chlorination rate. Under optimal conditions (temperature of 300 °C, holding time of 40 min, mass ratio of NH4Cl to steel slag of 2:1, and steel slag particle size of 75–106 μm), the calcium chlorination rate can reach 92.47%. Kinetic analysis based on the unreacted core shrinking model confirms that this chlorination process is controlled by the diffusion of the solid product layer. The resulting calcium-containing leachate, after carbonation precipitation, yields well-formed, uniformly shaped rhombohedral calcite particles.

item.title: Ultrasmall Superparamagnetic Fe 3 O 4 Nanoparticles Green-Synthesized with Cosmos caudatus : Phytochemical Surface Coordination and Suppression of MCF-7 Migration
item.description:
Abstract
Phytochemical-mediated synthesis of superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (SPION) is dominated by a narrow set of plant substrates, and extending this chemical space to phylogenetically distinct species remains an open question. Herein, we report the first application of Cosmos caudatus Kunth leaf extract, rich in quercetin glycosides, catechins, and chlorogenic acid, to the green sonochemical synthesis of superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (CC-SPION), benchmarked against an extract-free control (Bare-SPION). Acoustic cavitation combined with phytochemical reduction produced a crystalline inverse-spinel iron oxide in 25 min at near ambient temperature. TEM revealed near-monodisperse, semispherical primary particles of 7.30 ± 0.88 nm smaller than green-synthesized iron oxides in related studies; the TEM primary-particle diameter (7.30 nm) and XRD crystallite size (7.25 nm) were in close agreement, with FE-SEM reporting larger drying-induced aggregates (7.7–17.5 nm). Multipeak XRD analysis showed the crystallite size fell from 11.61 nm (Bare-SPION) to 7.25 nm (CC-SPION). Energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) corroborated the elemental compositions, whereas Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) substantiated the existence of Cosmos caudatus chemicals within the nanoparticle composition. This coordinated phytochemical corona raised the zeta-potential magnitude from −20.4 to −42.5 mV, conferring electrosteric stabilization (PDI ≈ 0.08). VSM confirmed superparamagnetism at 298 K (Ms = 43.99 emu/g; with no coercivity and remanence). CC-SPION was noncytotoxic to HEK-293 and MCF-7 cells across 31.25–500 μg Fe/mL (ISO 10993–5; viability ≥70%), reduced MCF-7 wound closure over 24–48 h, and showed dose-dependent cell association/localization. These findings establish C. caudatus sonochemistry as a route to mechanistically well-defined ultrasmall biocompatible SPION for prospective MRI and antimigratory applications.

item.title: Solution-Processed Ge 25 S 75 and Ge 25 Se 75 Thin Films─Influence of the Solution Preparation Pathway
item.description:
Abstract
Solution processing of chalcogenide thin films is an attractive alternative to vacuum-based deposition due to its low cost and scalability. We demonstrate a novel approach for preparing chalcogen-rich Ge–S and Ge–Se chalcogenide thin films from Ge33S67 and Ge33Se67 source bulk glasses by dissolving elemental chalcogen in the source bulk glass solution. This method allows for the preparation of chalcogen-rich thin films with a composition different from that of the source bulk glass. Two routes for chalcogen addition (the co-dissolution of bulk glass with chalcogen and the addition of chalcogen into a previously prepared bulk glass solution) were tested to study potential changes in dissolution chemistry and thus thin-film optical properties. The prepared solutions and deposited thin films were compared with the solutions and films produced by dissolving bulk glass of the targeted composition. Regardless of the preparation route, the solutions exhibited similar dissolution product structures, and the thin films possessed comparable composition, structure, and optical properties within the resolution and reproducibility of the applied methods, demonstrating the viability of both methods for the preparation of chalcogenide thin films. The presented method provides a new, simpler route for thin-film preparation.
